title: Federal and State Officials Ramp Up Scrutiny of DraftKings, Other Sports Betting Apps
content:
State and federal officials have ramped up scrutiny of online sports betting companies in recent weeks, launching inquiries, demanding information and, in one case, proposing a new rule that would limit when companies like DraftKings can pitch their users to bet more.

The moves — by gaming regulators, government lawyers and federal lawmakers — follow an investigation last month by ProPublica that tested the guardrails DraftKings and other sports betting companies have in place to protect users from spiraling out of control. That system is called responsible gaming, and executives say it’s integral to their companies’ long-term success.

The ProPublica article showed how DraftKings bestowed VIP status on a reporter who deliberately bet like a problem gambler. The report detailed the ways in which the app’s user design and promotions encouraged more betting — even after the reporter opted into responsible gaming tools designed to slow users down. A week earlier, The New York Times reported that DraftKings had used machine learning and artificial intelligence to target promotions to losing bettors.

title: How Ireland plans to beat the data center backlash
content:
TALLAGHT, Ireland — In a suburban industrial park south of Dublin, a sprawling mass of tubes, vents and steel stretches as far as the eye can see, forming a dense web of gray monoliths that encircle the city.

As the EU’s tech capital, where most of the world’s technology giants have their European headquarters, Ireland was ground zero for the backlash against the energy-guzzling data centers needed to power the promised revolution of artificial intelligence.

Dublin is now leading an experiment within Europe to force tech firms to invest in renewable energy. As pushback spreads across Europe and data centers prove a hot-button issue for the U.S. midterm elections, that puts Ireland at the vanguard of countries globally that are trying to quell voter anger over financial and environmental disruptions caused by data centers.

Back in 2021, Ireland was far ahead of the curve in slamming the brakes on data centers as its utilities regulator almost entirely halted new facilities connecting to the creaking electricity grid around Dublin. Authorities warned that the exploding data center industry posed a “significant” risk to the security of the country’s electricity supply.

title: Behind the Blog: Tech Support
content:
This is Behind the Blog, where we share our behind-the-scenes thoughts about how a few of our top stories of the week came together. This week, we discuss customer service and Proton fallout.

JASON: Since I wrote about ChatGPT turning me into tech support for people’s random problems, I have gotten many more AI-generated emails from people asking me to solve their tech support problems. So, mission accomplished I guess. I think and hope it was clear in the article, but I think this phenomenon is happening to a lot of journalists, not just us at 404 Media. A lot of the ChatGPT chats I saw told people to reach out to multiple journalists, and gave them contact info and instructions on how to do so. Some suggested that they reach out to lawyers or academic researchers as well, so I assume it’s all sorts of people who are getting this new type of spam.

title: Why Wikimedia Is Speaking Up in a Major AI Copyright Case
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation has filed an amicus brief, a “friend of the court” submission, with the Southern District Court of New York in In re: OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, a major copyright case involving OpenAI and Microsoft. The Foundation’s goal is to help protect the open, accessible knowledge that Wikipedia, and millions of people, depend on.

The case brings together 12 lawsuits, the most well-known of them being The New York Times Co. v Microsoft and OpenAI. At its heart is an important question: When AI companies use copyrighted information does it qualify as fair use?

For the Wikimedia Foundation, the answer needs to leave room for innovation while supporting the people and organizations that make access to knowledge possible, including Wikimedia volunteers. The Foundation is not taking the side of either OpenAI or The New York Times in this case. It is asking the court to protect open knowledge, something that matters to everyone who uses the internet.

title: January 2026 Protests: Milad Ebrahimi Sentenced to Prison and Fine
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Milad Ebrahimi has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.

The report states that Branch 101 of the Criminal Court II of Kamyaran issued a verdict against Ebrahimi, which was communicated to him on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Under the ruling, he was sentenced to one year of discretionary imprisonment and a fine of 400 million tomans on the charge of “disrupting public order.”

The court hearing concerning the charges against Ebrahimi was held in October of this year before the same judicial branch.

On February 1, 2026, Milad Ebrahimi was arrested alongside his brother, Hamed Ebrahimi, by security forces in Kamyaran and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Sanandaj. His arrest took place while he was recovering at home from injuries sustained during the protests in Kamyaran on the evening of January 8, 2026. During those protests, he had been struck in the lower back by live ammunition and subsequently underwent surgery at a hospital in Sanandaj.

title: Critic of Mali’s Junta Forcibly Disappeared Six Months On
content:
Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, an outspoken critic of Mali’s junta, and his son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, remain missing, their fate unknown, and the Malian authorities silent. Every day that passes without news raises fears for their safety and deepens their family’s anguish.

Unidentified gunmen abducted Tall in Bamako, Mali’s capital, on May 2. Tall’s son went missing on May 16 after receiving a call informing him that he could deliver belongings to his father, who was reportedly being held at an undisclosed location.

Radio France Internationale reported in July that the United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances had urged Mali’s authorities to locate and protect Tall and his son.

International media suggest that Malian intelligence services may be holding Tall in a secret facility. Malian authorities, however, have neither acknowledged detaining Tall or his son nor provided information about their location, legal status, or health, despite requests from Tall’s family and a legal team.

title: Apple Is Entering Its Slop Era
content:
My ears perked up when I heard Apple’s new foldable phones were cracking. I licked my lips when the company announced it’s releasing a touch-screen laptop. This was a company that once charged $19 for a polishing cloth, asked $200 for a VESA mount, and sold $700 wheels for the Mac Pro. Now it’s borrowing tired ideas from its competitors and launching hardware its previous leaders rejected.

The once dominant company is struggling to find its feet in an AI-driven post-Tim Cook world. John Ternus is the new CEO — a 25 year veteran of the company with a track record of pushing harebrained hardware schemes like the much reviled Touch Bar and lawsuit inducing butterfly keyboard. 

With Ternus at the helm, I feel there’s a good chance Apple’s best days are behind it, that it will have to make do with less, that it’s déclassé. Apple, blindsided by AI and relying on crowdpleasing hardware gimmicks, is downwardly mobile. It’s in its slop era. The company that once asked consumers to “Think Different” is now releasing hardware that’s just like everything else on the market.

title: From Wikipedia to the Wikimedia movement: making free knowledge easier to share
content:
What if sharing an interesting Wikimedia fact did not require a design tool, a QR-code generator and a separate caption? Wiki DYK Share Tool (wiki-dyk.toolforge.org) turns content from supported Wikimedia pages into ready-to-share images with QR codes, captions and customizable hashtags. It can also help communities promote campaigns, events and initiatives without requiring graphic-design skills.

In October 2025, the Wikimedia Foundation reported that human pageviews on Wikipedia had declined by approximately 8% compared with the same months in 2024. The Foundation pointed to changing online habits, including AI-generated answers in search engines and younger audiences increasingly turning to social video platforms for information. Read the Wikimedia Foundation’s update.

For those of us who contribute to Wikimedia projects, this raises an important question: how can we help more people discover the knowledge our communities create?

Every day, volunteers write articles, upload photographs, improve dictionaries, digitize historical documents, contribute structured data and organize community events. Yet much of this work remains unfamiliar to people outside our communities.

title: Helene Schjerfbeck ja Venny Soldan-Brofeldt – syksyn odotettu näyttely on avautunut Järvenpään taidemuseossa 29.10.2026–28.2.2027
content:
Järvenpään taidemuseon odotettu syksyn näyttely on avautunut. Näyttely tuo yhteen elinikäiset taiteilijaystävykset Helene Schjerfbeckin (1862–1946) ja Venny Soldan-Brofeldtin (1863–1945) ja erityisesti heidän erilaisten taiteilijapolkujensa kiinnostavat yhtymäkohdat, vaikutteet ja teemat. Schjerfbeckin ja Soldan-Brofeldtin taiteellista tuotantoa tarkastellaan näyttelyssä näin hyvin uusista näkökulmista.

Järvenpään taidemuseossa on Suomen kattavin Venny Soldan-Brofeldtin teoskokoelma. Hän asui Järvenpäässä vuosina 1897–1911 yhdessä kirjailija Juhani Ahon kanssa ja vaikutti keskeisesti Tuusulanjärven taiteilijayhteisön syntyyn.

Näyttelyn innoittajana toimii professori emerita Riitta Konttisen tietokirja Kunpa saisin hänen elämänsä (Siltala, 2024). title: Ghost in the machine: how AI is haunting the search for the supernatural
content:
Ghost hunting has changed in recent years due to AI chatbots, and paranormal enthusiasts are concerned

Ghost hunting is a tech-heavy pursuit. When Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting investigate haunted locations, they’re loaded up with software of their own design, such as an app that assigns signals from a phone’s sensors to different words in a database. In the age of ChatGPT, the ghost-hunting pair is probing the world of AI. They describe one of their latest inventions, an app called GhostTube Seer, as “the world’s first AI Ghost Hunting tool”.

In the hands of paranormal investigators, scientific tools like EMF meters (used to detect electromagnetic fields) are repurposed to identify changes and anomalies that they believe indicate supernatural activity. Seer is, in many ways, simply an expansion of that practice, another way to scan an empty room and believe that something may be there. The app, which requires a paid monthly subscription, has more than 1m downloads, according to its Google Play store listing.

title: Massive Fanfic Site Archive of Our Own Says It’s Going Down for 'Up to 4 Weeks'
content:
Archive of Our Own (AO3), a massive repository for fanfiction and creative writing, might be down for as long as a month after going down for "maintenance" on Thursday.

The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the non-profit organization that runs AO3, posted on its status page early Thursday morning that the site was down for maintenance. A few hours later, it updated the status to say that it was expected to take at least 12 hours. By Thursday afternoon, it said the site restoration will take around two weeks, but could take up to a month.

“We are hopeful that we will be able to bring the site back up in a degraded state sooner. If that does happen, there may be times when the site has to be brought down temporarily until this is fully resolved. Please stay tuned for further info,” OTW wrote.

title: Pakistan: Terrorism conviction of human rights lawyers an indictment of justice system
content:
Responding to the conviction and ten-year imprisonment of Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha today by the Anti-Terrorism Court in Islamabad, Yasmine Ahmed, Senior Director for Regional Human Rights Impact at Amnesty International, said:

“These convictions are an indictment of Pakistan’s justice system. This was not just Imaan and Hadi on trial, it was a test of the judiciary’s ability to uphold the principles of justice and the right to fair trial. It has failed that test miserably. It is clear that these ‘anti-terrorism’ charges are being used to punish Imaan and Hadi for their human rights advocacy.

“Imaan and Hadi have been consistently denied the right to an open and fair trial, which they were initially barred from attending in person. The trial was later shifted inside the prison premises where they were kept behind a cage-like structure during the hearings.

title: EU Satellite Imagery Delayed Over Gaza and Parts of West Bank by 24-hours
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. Become a member and support our work here.

Imagery captured by the European Space Agency’s freely available Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 satellites appears to be delayed over Gaza and parts of the West Bank, a Bellingcat analysis has found.

While the delay remains relatively short at just 24 hours, this can still impact the speed at which analysts and researchers can observe what is happening in the region.

For example, the Israeli Defence Forces demolished homes in the West Bank Palestinian city of Hebron in recent days. New imagery captured on October 26, which included Hebron, would allow open source researchers to quickly confirm the demolitions, assess the impacted area and observe any unreported IDF activity. But imagery for the western half of Hebron was not available until October 27 due to the Sentinel-2 delay, inhibiting real-time fact-checking and reporting on this evolving situation.

title: Experts: What China wants from the COP31 climate talks
content:
With the COP31 climate summit in Turkey looming, all eyes are on China to see what the country will push for in the negotiations.

At COP30 last year, China helped to secure a “dialogue” on climate-related “unilateral trade measures”, as well as a two-year “work programme” concerning climate finance.

The nation also championed south-south cooperation throughout the conference and co-led a summit on methane, alongside Brazil and the UK.

In a recent press conference, China’s environment vice-minister Li Gao noted the need to “uphold multilateralism” and send a “clear political signal” that the global community is united around climate action. 

Li also pledged to advocate for an “open and efficient” trade system that “facilitates” adoption of clean-energy technologies.

On the more traditional topics of mitigation and finance, Li highlighted the need to “address insufficient emission reduction efforts by developed countries and inadequate financial support” for developing countries.

Carbon Brief asked six leading experts on China what they believe China wants from COP31 and what signals they will be watching for. 

Their responses have been edited for length and clarity.

  • Kate Logan
  • Ma Jun 
  • Yao Zhe

title: Georgia – A Step Away From One-Party Rule
content:
Georgia’s Constitutional Court has begun hearing a lawsuit filed by ruling-party MPs to ban opposition groups. According to the official results of the disputed 2024 parliamentary election, four of the five targeted opposition forces received nearly 800,000 votes, or about 38% of valid ballots.

The implications extend far beyond these organizations. Legislation adopted in May 2025 allows the court to ban similar successor parties and requires it to rule on such cases within 14 days. Separate amendments permit permanent restrictions on the political participation of individuals “associated” with banned parties.

The aim is to strip the opposition of its ability to contest future elections. Bidzina Ivanishvili, Georgian Dream’s billionaire founder and the country’s de facto ruler, wants voters to conclude that no organized alternative to his rule exists, and that political change is impossible.

Even by Ivanishvili’s standards, the attempt to eliminate meaningful electoral competition marks an extraordinary low. The closest recent parallel, other than Russia, is Belarus’s liquidation of opposition parties in 2023 after it stole an election from the democratic opposition in 2020.

title: Meet AI Engineer Who Resigned from DeepMind over "Google's Complicity in the Gaza Genocide"
content:
Several tech workers at Google’s AI unit DeepMind have resigned in protest over the tech giant’s work with the U.S. and Israeli militaries. Last week, DeepMind research engineer Sofia Liguori announced her resignation in a letter to her colleagues titled “Stay Human.” She denounced what she called “Google’s complicity in the Gaza genocide” and the increasing integration of Google’s technology into military and surveillance systems.

“I felt I could not, in good faith, send this message of building AI to benefit humanity while ignoring that our company was complicit in a genocide,” Liguori tells Democracy Now! “The problem is that when the focus is on the model capabilities and on the potential for agents 'going rogue,' we are shifting the attention from a specific human choice … which is this unrestrained, unregulated integration of the systems without red lines.”

title: EKP päätti jälleen ohjauskorosta – energiasokin kaikki vaikutukset eivät vielä näy
content:
Euroopan keskuspankki (EKP) päätti pitää ohjauskorkonsa odotetusti ennallaan.

EKP:n neuvoston mukaan energian hinnat ovat jatkaneet nousuaan, mutta pohjainflaatio on pysynyt toistaiseksi jotakuinkin vakaana eivätkä palkat näytä reagoineen energiasokkiin merkittävästi.

Neuvosto arvioi lausunnossaan, että kaikki energiasokin vaikutukset eivät kuitenkaan ole vielä nähtävissä.

EUROALUEEN inflaatio kiihtyi syyskuussa 3,8 prosenttiin. Neuvosto toteaa, että se on sitoutunut keskipitkällä aikavälillä varmistamaan inflaation vakautumisen kahden prosentin tavoitteen mukaiseksi.

Talletuskorko pysyy 2,5 prosentissa, perusrahoitusoperaatioiden korko 2,65 prosentissa ja maksuvalmiusluoton korko 2,9 prosentissa.

Nordean pääanalyytikko Jan von Gerich katsoo, että koronnosto joulukuussa vaikuttaa yhä todennäköiseltä, vaikka hän pitää rahapolitiikkalausunnon sävyä pehmeämpänä kuin syyskuussa.

OP POHJOLAN seniorimarkkinaekonomisti Jari Hännikäinen sanoo analyysissaan, että vakaalla linjalla jatkamista puolsi epävarmuus euroalueen tulevasta talous- ja inflaatiokuvasta sekä nopeasti voimistuneet Ranskan politiikkariskit.

title: Tietoturvasääntely finanssialalla – vyö ja henkselit vai tuplasakot?
content:
Tietoturvan sääntely lisääntyy ja useampi valvontaviranomainen on kiinnostunut sen noudattamisen valvonnasta – kehityskulku, joka voi johtaa päällekkäisiin seuraamuksiin.

Tietoturvallisuuden sääntely on viime vuosina moninkertaistunut. Erityisen selvästi tietoturvavelvoitteiden moninaisuus näkyy finanssisektorilla, jota säännellään samanaikaisesti monien eri lakien, asetusten ja muiden säädösten nojalla. Sääntelyn lisääntyminen on johtanut myös päällekkäisyyksiin.

Päällekkäiset vaatimukset aiheuttavat tulkintaongelmia etenkin silloin, kun useammalla viranomaisella on rinnakkainen toimivalta ja sanktiointivalta samasta tapahtumasta. Tällaiset tilanteet voivat pahimmillaan johtaa moninkertaisiin rangaistuksiin samasta tosiasiallisesta menettelystä tai laiminlyönnistä.

Moninkertainen sääntely on johtanut yhä useammin tilanteisiin, joissa enemmän kuin yksi viranomainen tarkastelee samaa tapahtumasarjaa eri lainsäädännön näkökulmasta.

title: Tech Tips for Parents this Digital Parenting Week
content:
In today’s digital world, the internet is an essential resource for young people to access information, explore community, and find themselves. But we know that this often comes alongside fears of experiencing online harms like doxxing, grooming, or bullying.

Trying to protect your family from everything all the time is impractical and exhausting, but some thoughtful planning can help families devise a workable plan that meets their needs and addresses their concerns.

That’s why this Digital Parent Week, we’re sharing easy tips on how parents and their children can work together to co-curate a digital safety plan that helps all members of the family enjoy the benefits of technology while protecting their online privacy and safety. 

Online safety begins with communication, not just restrictions. Talk with a young person about how they use the internet: their favourite apps, games, and social media platforms for example. Creating a supportive environment helps young people feel comfortable asking for help if something goes wrong online.

title: The Cuban Regime Didn't Just Interrupt a UN Event. It Validated Its Own Central Premise.
content:
US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz reacts to Cuban diplomats following the Cuba Libre event. (Photo Credit: US Mission to the United Nations)

At a United Nations event last week, the Cuban regime proved its critics right.

On October 19, diplomats, UN officials, and journalists gathered in New York to hear directly from brave Cubans whose lives have been shaped by political imprisonment, censorship, forced exile, and repression. They came to discuss what happens in Cuba when citizens peacefully exercise their fundamental rights.

By the end of the event, they had their answer.

What unfolded at the United Nations was instantly recognizable to many Cubans. Cuba's permanent representative to the UN, Ernesto Soberón Guzmán, and other government representatives crowded the entrances and hallways outside the meeting room, filming attendees, including the organizer, US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz, shouting accusations and branding regime critics “terrorists” and “liars.” The scene mirrored the harassment and smear campaigns that the regime has long deployed against its opponents.

title: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence Against Mohammad Naderi
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence against Mohammad Naderi has been upheld. Based on information received by HRANA, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence of Mohammad Naderi, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “espionage.”

An informed source close to Naderi’s family told HRANA: “Using Starlink satellite internet, photographing certain locations, and sending images to media outlets abroad were among the allegations brought against him and served as the basis for his death sentence.”

Naderi was arrested by security forces in Tehran on March 17, 2026, amid war-related security developments, and transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison. He was subsequently transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in October of this year.

title: Women Should Never Give Birth in Shackles
content:
An incarcerated Indigenous woman was reportedly shackled during a hospital stay earlier this month to deliver her baby by caesarean section in a Queensland hospital in Australia.

Queensland Corrective Services promised an internal review but did not confirm the shackling. Shackling a woman during childbirth contravenes international human rights standards.

The incident happened days before Australia’s two major political parties blocked a vote in parliament on October 14 on a bill to ban the shackling of prisoners during childbirth. United Nations human rights experts criticized the Australian parliament’s failure to vote on the bill.

Prisoners and detainees do not lose their rights to health or to be treated humanely and with dignity. Restraining a woman during childbirth raises grave concerns about degrading treatment and interference with care, which constitute obstetric violence.

Obstetric violence is the physical and emotional abuse of pregnant people seeking sexual and reproductive health services and information, including maternal health. It is a form of gender-based violence and a violation of fundamental human rights.

title: Weaving ‘Tapestries’: Introducing A New Tool for Digital Storytelling and Archiving
content:
Between text, images, audio clips and videos, there are so many elements at your fingertips to tell a story in the digital era. A new expressive tool is now available to make it easy to assemble material online and share your creation widely.

Tapestries is a user interface developed by Bob Stein and Dan Visel (who works on the Wayback team) that allows people to make dynamic, multi-linear presentations with various digital objects. The curation tool lets users gather items from all over the web and put them together into a single space to tell a story. Rather than simply listing links at the end of a document, a tapestry can be designed by dragging photos, video clips or other items onto a digital canvas that viewers can click to open.

The finished product can be kept private or posted publicly – with the option of inviting others to collaborate, comment on the project, or make copies of the tapestry to edit and revise.

The Tapestries platform launched as part of the Internet Archive’s Oct. 21 celebration. Stein, Visel, as well as the project’s new director, Ben Vershbow, were on hand to demonstrate the tool during the Funston Avenue party.

title: Public consultations open for draft African digital governance guidelines
content:
The African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights (ACHPR) has published the first drafts of two landmark African Guidelines on continental digital governance, developed with the support of UNESCO. 

Now open for broad public consultations and stakeholder comments, these guidelines represent a milestone in embedding African realities and perspectives into global digital regulatory frameworks.

This milestone is championed by a key member of the M20 – Moxii Africa (formerly Media Monitoring Africa) and SOS Support Public Broadcasting Coalition, which is a co-signatory to the  Johannesburg Declaration. 

Moxii and SOS have been instrumental driving forces behind the continental push for information integrity, media viability, and platform accountability.

The importance of framing issues of information integrity around Global South realities is a central thrust of the Johannesburg Declaration. When it comes to Artificial Intelligence, for instance, the declaration calls for recognition that sustainable development in Africa requires robust accountability mechanisms that prevent the entrenchment of technological dependencies.

title: Developed for the public sector and kept public: explaining open source licensing
content:
We’ve copied this post from the blog of mySociety’s commercial subsidiary SocietyWorks. It’s part 2 in their Responsible Tech series, in which they explore open source technology and data privacy, security, and sovereignty. In this update, Chloe Carrington Dunn explains what open source licensing is, how to spot it and what public sector decision-makers need to know about it.

— 

The first post in this series explored the benefits of open and reusable source code. Angela Dixon, our Managing Director, made the case that “if it is the product of public spend, then it should be built to be reused and shared” and busted some of the myths around open source being more vulnerable to maleficent actors or less secure. 

If you didn’t read that first post, the tl;dr was this: publishing open source code can reduce risk, prevent vendor lock-in, and means the benefits of the code can be shared among other public sector entities. 

But not everyone understands what open source means and how to recognise when something is open source. In this blog post, I’ll clear up when open source code is used, what it means to be open, and what this means for the public sector.

title: Criminal Probe Launched in South Africa Over Contraband Baobabs Bound for Georgia
content:
South African authorities have opened a criminal investigation into the attempted illegal export of five baobab trees to Georgia, halting a massive shipment at the coastal port of Durban after discovering the exporter lacked required environmental permits.

The five trees, estimated to be between 200 and 300 years old and weighing up to 30 tons each, remain impounded at a Durban logistics warehouse while investigators build a case under the country's forestry laws.

Under South Africa’s National Forests Act, the indigenous baobab is a protected species. It is illegal to cut down, harvest, transport, or export live specimens without explicit authorization from environmental regulators. While South Africa permits the commercial trade of processed baobab derivatives—such as fruit powder, seed oil, and cosmetic extracts—under strict licensing, the live specimen trade is tightly restricted to protect the slow-growing trees from international exploitation.

title: The Early Years of Electronic Pop: The Moog Craze, Psychedelic Experiments, and More
content: There’s a decent chance you’ve heard at least a couple of tracks from Wendy Carlos’ Switched-On Bach. But when was the last time you put on Switched-On Rock, Switched-On Country, Switched-On Santa, or Switched-On Bacharach? More likely than not, you’ve never even heard of those other albums, which have nothing to do with Carlos and everything to do with the music-industry fad that her then-high-tech renditions of Bach set off in the late nineteen-sixties and early seventies. That’s the subject of the new Bandsplaining video above, which covers the “awkward and glorious” releases that constituted the initial waves of electronic pop music.

title: OpenWebSearch ON AIR!
content:
“Nachschub: Offene Infrastrukturen sollen den Datenmangel für KI-Systeme beheben” (New Developments: Open Infrastructures aim to address the data shortage for AI Systems)”– that was the title of a report on Deutschlandfunk on October 17, which mentioned, among other things, the OpenWebSearch initiative.

A study by the Pew Research Center in August 2026 found that 10% of English-language content on the web today is generated by AI or has been processed using AI. For websites published after 2022, that figure is already as high as 35%. For a long time, the web was an important source for obtaining AI training data, but access to open data is becoming more difficult and scarce. While large AI providers can now afford access to data through licensing deals, small providers are falling by the wayside, the report continues.

The report emphasises the importance of human-generated data for training AI and highlights the OpenWebSearch.EU project, “which aims to preserve and keep accessible high-quality, human-generated web data.”

It’s worth a listen! The episode is available here (in German).

title: Search More Than 500 Cases of U.S. Citizens Detained by Immigration Agents
content:
Experts have long warned that immigration dragnets will inevitably result not only in the erosion of rights for immigrants but also for citizens. Since the start of this Trump administration, we’ve watched those warnings come true. 

So we have once again done what the government won’t: We have tallied and cataloged every case we can find of an immigration agent reportedly detaining a citizen during the current administration — more than 500 cases from Inauguration Day through Oct. 21, 2026. 

Read our earlier reporting on U.S. citizens being detained.

We compiled our list by scouring social media, court records and local media, and we included an incident only if we could find at least two sources for it. We asked the Department of Homeland Security about each incident, and we searched for any federal criminal charges that were brought in relation to each incident. (DHS has repeatedly said it is not arresting U.S. citizens.)

Since the government itself does not track these cases, our list is almost certainly an undercount. Below, we’re showing you every case we found — the reality that the administration denies — along with the receipts. Read more about how we reported this project.

title: Digital Independence Day: Messaging your audience
content:
As an organisation, you want to be easy to reach for your target group or audience. That’s why many organisations use messaging apps, alongside being reachable by phone or email. But that’s not their only function: messaging is also widely used for collaboration and for maintaining communities.

Mention messaging, and many people immediately think of WhatsApp. With more than 13 million users in the Netherlands, it’s the most widely used communication app and, for many people, the platform for staying in touch. Unfortunately, using WhatsApp does come with some downsides. WhatsApp is owned by Meta, the company that’s also behind Facebook and Instagram. Meta’s main business model is selling personalised advertising, and to do that as effectively as possible, it wants to collect as much information as possible about everyone. Messages in one-to-one chats are encrypted by default, so Meta can’t easily read along, but that protection isn’t there for group chats or chats linked to a helpdesk or support system. And even without reading the messages, Meta can infer all kinds of personal information from usage data.

So this month, we’re looking at alternatives for: chat tools.

content:
Valtiovarainministeriö julkisti maanantaina 26.10. meno- ja rakenneselvityksensä, jossa eritellään erilaisia sopeutusvaihtoehtoja seuraavalle vaalikaudelle sekä arvioita näiden vaikutuksista julkiseen talouteen. Selvityksessä on mukana vaihtoehtoja, jotka heikentäisivät merkittävästi kuvataiteilijoiden toimintaedellytyksiä.

Mahdollisina sopeutuskohteina meno- ja rakenneselvityksessä nostetaan esiin kolme etenkin kuvataiteilijoihin kohdistuvaa kohdetta:

  • Uusien taiteilijaeläkkeiden myöntämisen lopettaminen (säästö realisoituisi VM:n arviossa hyvin hitaasti, mutta saavuttaisi lopulta n. 24 milj. euroa)

title: Så stödjer Svenska institutet ukrainska kommuners återuppbyggnad
content:
Medan kriget pågår behöver Ukrainas kommuner hantera akuta problem samtidigt som de planerar för långsiktig återuppbyggnad. Många kommuner har också förlorat personal och därmed viktig kompetens. Mot den bakgrunden finns en efterfrågan på expertis, kunskapsutbyte och stöd i planeringsarbetet. Genom det SI-finansierade samarbetet har kommunerna därför fått tillgång till svenska och ukrainska experter inom bland annat stadsplanering och samhällsviktig service, och kunnat utbyta erfarenheter kring sina utmaningar. Det har i sin tur bidragit till att de kunnat ta fram förslag på åtgärder utifrån respektive kommuns behov när det gäller vattenförsörjning, energi, avfallshantering, bostäder och lokal utveckling.

Ett exempel är kommunen Lozova i den krigsdrabbade Charkivregionen. Genom det svensk-ukrainska samarbetet har kommunen fått kontakt med Swedfund, som nu finansierar en förstudie om hur kommunens vatten- och avloppssystem kan moderniseras.

Ytterligare fem ukrainska kommuner har arbetat med lokala behov inom bland annat vattenförsörjning, energi och avfallshantering. Genom samarbetet har de också knutit kontakter med organisationer som kan bidra i det fortsatta arbetet.

title: Carney frames C$1.6B AI investment as national security imperative
content:
MONTREAL — Prime Minister Mark Carney is positioning Ottawa’s C$1.6 billion investment in Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere as a downpayment on his country’s national security. 

“We’re not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know or … don’t trust,” Carney said Thursday in Montreal ahead of the start of the Canada-EU summit.

Carney framed the upcoming congress, which includes meetings Friday with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa, as a shared endeavor to build a stronger transatlantic alliance in the face of global disruption.

“Sovereignty now requires secure access to semiconductors, critical minerals, payment systems, clean energy technology, vaccines, space-based communications and artificial intelligence,” Carney said. “Canada is taking a major step forward in artificial intelligence.”

In a pre-summit speech earlier Thursday in Montreal, von der Leyen cited April’s multi-billion dollar merger between Cohere and German counterpart Aleph Alpha as a key piece of the deepening Canada-EU cooperation that is set to unfold at Friday’s talks on AI.

title: Musiikinkuuntelu Suomessa 2026: musiikki yhdistää suomalaisia epävarmassa ajassa – suomenkielinen pop säilytti asemansa suosituimpana musiikkityylinä
content:
Musiikki on suomalaisille edelleen poikkeuksellisen tärkeä osa elämää: jopa 91 prosenttia pitää musiikkia erittäin tai jokseenkin tärkeänä kokien sen tuovan iloa, elämyksiä ja yhteyttä muihin ihmisiin. Samalla suomalaiset arvostavat vahvasti kotimaista musiikkia ja suhtautuvat varauksellisesti tekoälyn tekemään musiikkiin. Tämä käy ilmi Musiikkituottajat – IFPI Finlandin ja Teoston Musiikinkuuntelu Suomessa 2026 -tutkimuksesta.

Tutkimuksen mukaan 51 prosenttia suomalaisista pitää musiikkia erittäin tärkeänä ja 40 prosenttia jokseenkin tärkeänä itselleen. Musiikista saa merkittävästi iloa elämäänsä 85 prosenttia suomalaisista, ja 76 prosenttia kokee sen tarjoavan syviä elämyksiä.

Musiikin merkitys korostuu erityisesti epävarmoina aikoina. Peräti 71 prosenttia suomalaisista kertoo musiikin olevan erityisen tärkeää silloin, kun elämässä on vaikeaa.

title: Spain’s high-speed train network is plagued by old signalling systems. They may have caused the deadly crash
content:
Shortly after 8am, two high-speed trains set off from Madrid’s Atocha station bound for Seville Santa Justa, but neither reached their destination. A failure in the LZB system – an automatic safety, signalling and protection system that monitors trains’ movement and activates automatic emergency braking – triggered a chain of events that led to a fatal accident, which killed 69 people and left many more injured.

Across the EU’s rail network, which spans almost 227,000km, there are more than 25 different, non-interoperable railway signalling systems. These systems (which include the German LZB, the French Crocodile, the Italian BACC and the Spanish ASFA) control and enable the safe movement of trains via blocks, sections of the track that can only have one train on them at any given moment.

On the Andalusia–Madrid line, the German LZB signalling system remains in operation, pending its replacement by the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS) that is already in place on other, more modern lines.

The ERTMS specifications are set out in EU legislation. The aim is for this system to completely replace national ones across the entire EU by 2050.

title: How porn became so extreme – and how it’s shaping the sex lives of young people
content:
A few years ago, the singer Billie Eilish opened up on the Howard Stern Show about how she began watching porn around age 11.

“I’m so angry that porn is so loved, and I’m so angry at myself for thinking that it was ok,” she said.

Eilish became addicted to porn, and it led to problems. “The first few times I had sex, I was not saying no to things that were not good,” she said. She had nightmares because the content she was watching was so violent and abusive.

Online porn is a multi-million dollar business, driven by algorithms designed to keep people clicking for more. These algorithms push more and more extreme content, often for free, to people who didn’t go searching for it. This can include strangulation, exploitation or incest porn, that’s often misogynistic and racist too.

“If you take incest and strangulation, we can look at content studies from the 1980s, for example, when there was hardly any of that material,” Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University in the UK, tells The Conversation Weekly podcast. “Today both incest and strangulation becomes mainstream.”

title: Australian heritage: A letter from Bologna
content:
Aboriginal painting on rock surfaces. Photo: Herbert Basedow, Public domain. Source: National Museum of Australia via Wikimedia Commons

By Olivia Panetta*

In May 2020, Rio Tinto legally destroyed two rock shelters at Juukan Gorge in the Pilbara region.  The shelters preserved evidence of approximately 46,000 years of occupation and held profound  cultural significance for the Puutu Kunti Kurrama and Pinikura peoples. Australian legislation made this destruction entirely legal. It occurred specifically under ministerial consent granted through Western Australia’s Aboriginal Heritage Act 1972. That is perhaps the most disturbing part: a place of extraordinary cultural importance and memory could be recognised and recorded and still  the law enabled a mining company more authority over the site than it gave the people to whom the place belonged. A parliamentary inquiry followed, recommending a national framework built on free, prior and informed consent. More than six years later, such reform has not yet been enacted.

title: Serbian opiskelijaliike juhlii vaalivoittoa, mutta moni serbialainen ei koe demokratiaa tai EU:ta omakseen
content:
Serbian opiskelijaliike päihitti autokraattisen Aleksandar Vučićin SNS-puolueen parlamenttivaaleissa viime sunnuntaina lupaamalla loppua korruptiolle ja demokratian romuttamiselle. Uudesta linjasta huolimatta demokraattista Serbiaa ei kannata odotella EU:hun lähiaikoina, sillä opiskelijaliikke tulee kohtaamaan vaalikaudellaan hyvin jakautuneen ja demokratiakriittisen kansan sekä vaikutusvaltaa havittelevan Venäjän. EU:n kannattaa kuitenkin tarttua tilaisuuteen tarjota apuaan demokratian tukemisessa, vaikkei EU-jäsenyys olekaan Serbian prioriteetti. 

Viime sunnuntaina 25.10. serbialaisten opiskelijoiden kahden vuoden protestointi valtionhallinnon korruptiota, autoritaarista kehitystä ja kansan näköalattomuutta vastaan huipentui, kun liikkeen ehdokaslista Studentska lista syrjäytti 14 vuotta hallinneen presidentti Aleksandar Vučićin populistisen Serbian edistyspuolueen (SNS) 52,45 % äänisaaliilla. Vučić hajotti maan parlamentin syyskuussa hakeakseen uudelleen pääministeriksi  toisen presidenttikautensa loppuessa.

title: Tietoturvan suunnannäyttäjä -tunnustus annettiin työstä pankkitunnuskalastelujen estämiseksi
content:
Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin jakaman Tietoturvan suunnannäyttäjä -tunnustuksen sai tänä vuonna OP Pohjolan Principal IT Security Specialist Tuomas Kaijanen.

Traficom jakaa vuosittain tunnustuksen esimerkillisestä tietoturvaa edistävästä työstä. Tunnustus jaettiin nyt kymmenettä kertaa.

Tänä vuonna tunnustuksen sai Tuomas Kaijanen OP Pohjolasta. Tuomas Kaijasen sinnikäs työ on tuottanut pankkihuijausten torjuntaa tehostavan yhteistyömallin, jonka avulla pankit, teleoperaattorit ja viranomaiset ovat onnistuneet merkittävästi vähentämään pankkitunnuskalastelun uhrimääriä.

Pilotointivaihe saatiin päätökseen huhtikuussa 2025 ja seuraavaksi uutta mallia kehitetään kansalliseksi ratkaisuksi, josta hyötyy koko yhteiskunta.

title: Kansallisoopperan Figaron häät on ilo silmälle ja korvalle
content:
Tuulikki Närhinsalo

Anna Kelon ohjaama W.A. Mozartin ooppera Figaron häät sopii aivan kaikille ja erityisesti niille, jotka vieroksuvat epookista irrotettuja moderneja ohjauksia.

Pierre Beaumarchaisin näytelmä, johon ooppera perustuu, syntyi vain vähän ennen Ranskan vallankumousta ja aiheutti kohun satiirisella yhteiskuntakritiikillään.

Oopperan hilpeä alkusoitto on loistava soiva logo teokselle. Siinä kuuluu se riehakkaaksi yltyvä nopeiden tapahtumien ketju, jossa kolmen pariskunnan ja yhden hormonihöyryissään kiehuvan hovipojan kohtalot kietoutuvat toisiinsa aiheuttaen väärinkäsitysten, pettymysten, kiukun, koston ja vahingonilon vyöryn.

Anna Kelon ohjaama esitys on kyllin vauhdikas ja visuaalisesti kauniisti kiinni epookissa, raikkaasti maustettuna. Erika Turusen puvustustaide on luonut silmää hivelevän kauniita, näyttäviä asuja, joissa kangasta ei ole säästetty. Jani Uljaan lavastus on komea ja sopivan tyylitellysti realistinen: huoneet ovat huoneita, kalusteet kalusteita. Tumma, sinisen ja vihreän sävyttämä väriskaala ihastuttaa.

title: PHP und Wikipedia zeigen: Das Internet ist ohne Ehrenamt undenkbar
content:
Kannten Sie PHP vor dem 20. Oktober? Wikipedia weiß, dass es sich dabei um eine Skriptsprache für Webseiten handelt. Der Entwickler Rasmus Lerdorf hat sie 1995 als „Personal Home Page Tool“ für sich entwickelt – und dem Rest der Welt als freie Software zur Verfügung gestellt.

30 Jahre später ist PHP in über 70 % der Webseiten verbaut. Seit 2021 kümmert sich unter anderem die PHP-Stiftung darum, die freie Software zu pflegen. Sie gab am 20. Oktober bekannt, dass zwei Sicherheitslücken geleakt wurden, noch bevor bereits geplante Patches – also Flicken – zur Verfügung gestellt werden konnten.

Hunderte Millionen Webseiten waren nun potenziell verwundbar. Denn PHP steckt in vielen digitalen Produkten von Software-Firmen: In E-Commerce-Anwendungen für Online-Shops, in Content-Management-Systemen für Webseiten, in Blog-Plattformen oder Kommunikationsdiensten. Wer die Sicherheitslücke ausnutzen wollte – und über die technischen Fähigkeiten verfügt – konnte sich in die Webseiten hacken.

title: Poland is ditching coal. What happens to its miners?
content: Coal has long been synonymous with Polish energy. Just 20 years ago, 91% of Poland's electricity came from coal. Today, that figure has fallen to around 50%, while wind and solar power account for a quarter of the country's electricity generation. That's a major step forward for a country that started its energy transition from one of the most coal-dependent positions in the EU. Since 2006, Poland’s power-sector emissions have fallen by 30% despite a growing economy and rising electricity demand. That's encouraging news, particularly for southern Poland where some areas have long struggled with poor air quality. One of them is Kraków, my new home. From Kraków – a city that has transformed itself and left much of its smoggy past behind – I travelled north to the Baltic coast, where Poland's energy transition is truly taking off. At the beginning of October, all 76 turbines were installed at Poland's first offshore wind farm. Once fully operational, the wind farm is expected to generate enough electricity to power around 1.5 million homes and meet around 3% of the country's annual electricity demand. title: Finding the claims worth checking: How AI-assisted monitoring can support fact-checking journalism
content:
One of the major challenges facing fact-checking newsrooms is identifying the claims that deserve investigation in the first place. With misleading statements scattered across social media, podcasts, television and radio, journalists cannot possibly monitor everything. NORDIS has during the last two years been testing how AI-assisted monitoring can help address this challenge.

For fact-checkers, verifying a claim is only part of the job. Before journalists can investigate whether a statement is true, misleading or false, they first need to discover it.

This has become increasingly difficult as public debate takes place across a growing number of digital platforms, some of which are difficult to monitor systematically. Even traditional, lengthy political debates in parliaments and discussions on television and radio programmes generate hours of content containing potentially checkable statements.

NORDIS has for the last couple of years been testing and using technology developed by Norwegian company Factiverse to explore how automated monitoring can support editorial research and help journalists identify claims they might otherwise miss.

title: NATO – Stop Training for Yesterday’s Wars
content:
Ukrainian soldiers returning from NATO training programs in Britain or Poland sometimes discover that lessons learned abroad require immediate revision. The problem is not necessarily the quality of Western instruction, but the assumptions behind it.

Much of the alliance’s small-unit training still reflects conflicts in Iraq and Afghanistan, where Western forces enjoyed air superiority, technological advantages, and relatively reliable evacuation and resupply. Ukraine demonstrates what happens when these advantages disappear.

The modern battlefield has become almost entirely transparent, with reconnaissance drones, thermal imaging, electronic surveillance, and first-person-view (FPV) strike drones fundamentally changing infantry operations. Traditional squad formations, vehicle movements, and defensive positions can be detected and attacked within minutes.

Ukrainian units increasingly disperse into smaller groups, sometimes operating in teams of two or three rather than conventional squad formations. Concentration, once essential for command and maneuver, now creates vulnerability.

title: Stan Veuger: An uneasy transatlantic truce
content:
The second Trump administration has done significant damage to the transatlantic relationship, which is now marked by suspicion and frustration. The economic side of the relationship is no exception. After the dramatic disruption of Liberation Day, when President Trump announced the imposition of unlawful 20% tariffs on imports from the European Union, the EU and the US negotiated their way to a truce that has now been in place for a bit over a year.

The terms of the truce are lopsided. Under the framework agreed at Turnberry in July 2025, the United States applied a 15% ceiling, inclusive of existing duties, to most imports from the EU, though steel, aluminum, and copper stayed at 50%. The EU, for its part, agreed to eliminate its tariffs on American industrial goods, open its market to a list of agricultural and seafood products, and shelve the €93 billion package of countermeasures it had prepared. The average American tariff on European goods, below 2% a year earlier, is now close to 10%; the average European tariff on American goods approaches zero. Europe accepted this agreement—inconceivable just a year earlier—as the price of stability.

title: "She Was a Fighter": Dolores Huerta, Legendary Farmworker Organizer & Activist, Dies at 96
content:
Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.

In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

title: Dittmar & Indrenius thesis award for a thesis on human rights issues in medical artificial intelligence
content:
Dittmar & Indrenius has presented its annual thesis award to the master’s thesis in business law recognised by the Faculty of Law at the University of Helsinki as the most outstanding among those completed in 2025.

This year’s thesis award goes to Anni Paakkari for her master’s thesis “International Human Rights Law and Algorithmic Discrimination in Medical Artificial Intelligence”.

“The thesis skilfully bridges technical AI expertise and legal-political insight, offering a critical, well-sourced examination of how algorithmic bias in medical AI challenges international human rights law,” says Juli Mansnérus, Partner at Dittmar & Indrenius.

Warm congratulations to Anni Paakkari on an excellent master’s thesis!

At a ceremony held at Dittmar & Indrenius, the award was presented by Jukka Mähönen, Dean of the Faculty of Law at the University of Helsinki, and Partner Juli Mansnérus from Dittmar & Indrenius.

The thesis award is presented annually to a thesis in business law selected by the Faculty for its outstanding academic merit. Dittmar & Indrenius has presented this award since 1998.

title: The internet should not demand constant self-defence: Fairness starts before the click
content:
A fair digital environment cannot – and should not – depend on everyone being permanently alert. Fairness must be built into the environment itself, not left to the skills of the people using it. In practice, that means rules, not appeals: cancelling must be as easy as subscribing, protection must be the default rather than a setting, and a system that detects a moment of weakness must not be allowed to act on it.

title: Family Members Speak: The Toll of Political Imprisonment
content:
In his final public statement, Chinese Nobel Peace Prize laureate Liu Xiaobo wrote to his wife: “I am serving my sentence in a tangible prison, while you wait in the intangible prison of the heart.” His words capture the often-overlooked suffering of families who grapple with emotional anguish, mounting legal fees, and fears for their loved ones’ health and safety. Many find themselves thrust into the unfamiliar role of advocate, fighting for due process, visitation rights, and even basic information about those held incommunicado.

Solidarity with political prisoners must also extend to the families who endure these hardships. Below, they share their experiences in their own words.

Talia Khattak, daughter of political prisoner Idris Khattak

Every morning I wake up and try to carry on with my life, and every night the constant worry returns, and my heart drops: my father was convicted in a fake trial, he is getting old and sick, and he is not receiving his medicine. I lie awake wondering if he is in pain, if he knows how hard we are fighting for him. I should be caring for him now, yet I can’t hear his voice telling me it’s going to be okay.
snippet: In his final public statement, Chinese Nobel Peace Prize laureate Liu Xiaobo wrote to his wife: “I am serving my sentence in a tangible prison, while you wait in the intangible prison of the heart.”

title: A Myanmar journalist’s reflection: ‘When other people’s pain becomes part of you’
content:
An Exile Hub fellow shares their personal experiences and reflections

Originally published on Global Voices

Image from Exile Hub. Used with permission.

Exile Hub is one of Global Voices’ partners in Southeast Asia, emerging in response to the 2021 coup in Myanmar, and focusing on empowering journalists and human rights defenders. This article by a fellow of Exile Hub was published on August 15, 2026, and an edited version is republished under a content partnership agreement.

“Can I keep doing this work?”

I have asked myself that question more times than I can count.

When I first entered journalism as a young person, I was full of energy, conviction, and dreams. I believed journalism was a way to uncover the truth and to make sure people’s voices were heard.

Four years later, I began to realize that somewhere along the way, I was slowly losing parts of myself.

When I was 19, I never imagined that the career I chose would become both my livelihood and one of the reasons the road home would feel so far away.

content:

Under the ruling, the 21-year-old was sentenced to death on charges of “moharebeh” (waging war against God).

Omran Amani, a native of Kurdistan Province, had previously moved to Tehran in search of employment. He was arrested by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026 and is currently held in the Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is investigating further details regarding the specific allegations underlying the charge against him and the legal proceedings in his case.

title: Mbappé, Mao, and La Liga
content:
This week a Chinese sports forum unearthed an April 2026 interview with Real Madrid football star Kylian Mbappé jokingly likening himself to a “Chinese dictator” (dictateur chinois). While Mbappé, known for dictating terms on the pitch, did not name names, the broadcaster added art showing him as Chinese Communist Party founder Mao Zedong.

Beijing’s reaction was swift. China’s Foreign Ministry claimed the words “hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.” Chinese state broadcaster CCTV blacked out all Spanish football league La Liga matches.

The Chinese Communist Party under Xi Jinping has low tolerance for anything that could be interpreted as an affront to China, even a comment about Mao made in jest. Javier Tebas, the Spanish football league’s president, issued an apology praising La Liga’s ties with China’s “government departments.”

title: Latecomers Crowd the Race for the Next UN Chief
content:
UAE candidate Lana Nusseibeh faces questions over Sudan as Türkiye weighs a last-minute entry by former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 29 October 2026 (IDN) — The contest to succeed António Guterres as United Nations Secretary-General should be moving toward a decision by now. Instead, it is growing more crowded—and harder to predict.

Six informal polls among Security Council members have failed to produce a candidate acceptable to all five permanent members. Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica has often led the field, but she has not escaped opposition from veto-holding countries. Nor has any other contender.

The deadlock has opened the door to latecomers.

The United Arab Emirates nominated Lana Zaki Nusseibeh on 21 October, little more than two months before Guterres leaves office. Türkiye is now considering nominating Feridun Hadi Sinirlioğlu, a former foreign minister and UN ambassador who currently heads the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE).

content: Tässä tutkimuksessa analysoimme sellaisia verkkokeskusteluja, joissa tieteeseen liittyviä käsityksiä pyritään korjaamaan tai oikaisemaan. Tavoitteenamme on muodostaa parempi ymmärrys siitä, miten tieteeseen liittyviä käsityksiä rakennetaan tiedemyönteisten keskustelijoiden verkkokeskusteluissa nykyisen polarisoituneen asenneilmapiirin aikana. Keskitymme erityisesti siihen, millaisia tiedekäsityksiä tiedemyönteisten keskustelijoiden verkkokeskusteluviesteissä ilmenee sekä millaisin kielellisin keinoin keskustelijat rakentavat ja vahvistavat tiedekäsityksiään. Aineistonamme on Suomi24-keskustelupalstasta keskusteluista koottu Suomi24-korpus, josta eristimme sellaiset vuosina 2018–2020 kirjoitetut viestit, joissa mainittiin tiede-sana. Analyysissamme keskitymme tiede ei ole X, vaan -muotin sisältäviin viesteihin ja niissä ilmeneviin tiedekäsityksiin. Tutkimuksemme osoittaa, että tiedekäsitykset jäsentyvät kolmeen pääluokkaan: tiede on uuden ja varman tiedon hankintaa, tiede on objektiivista ja tiede on julkista ja sidoksissa yhteiskuntaan. title: Iraqi MP Gets Six Years, $20M Fine for Oil Graft
content:
A specialized anti-corruption court in Iraq sentenced lawmaker Muthanna al-Samarrai to six years in prison and ordered him to repay nearly $20 million for exploiting his position to profit from state oil contracts.

Al-Samarrai, who heads the Sunni political bloc Azm Alliance, used his parliamentary oversight role to benefit from public works and procurement deals involving the state-owned North and South Refineries companies. The lawmaker played a direct role in awarding contracts and steering payments to associates through four private companies, according to Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission. The court ordered him to return 30 billion Iraqi dinars ($19.81 million) in illicit gains following his arrest in June 2026 alongside a former deputy oil minister.

title: Surreal Pinscreen Animations Bring Kafka, Gogol & Mussorgsky to Life (1933–1972)
content:
What do Franz Kafka, Nikolai Gogol, and Modest Mussorgsky have in common? They stand alone among their peers for their darkly humorous sensibilities, fascination with the grotesque, imaginative takes on cultural traditions, and a predisposition for the proto-surreal. Like the odd figure lurching through the first movement of Mussorgsky’s Pictures at an Exhibition, they are gnomic artists: enigmatic and ambiguous, given to the aphoristic in stories and tone poems of monstrous and marvelous beings. It’s easy to imagine the three of them, or their works at least, in cryptic conversation with each other.

We might imagine that conversation as we watch three works by these major European artists—all of which we’ve featured on the site before—animated via the painstaking pinscreen method pioneered by husband-and-wife, Russian-and-French duo Alexander Alexeieff and Claire Parker.

The two invented the technique in the 1930s. Dedicated to this extremely labor-intensive process, they made 6 short films over a period of 50 years, including adaptations of Kafka’s “Before the Law,” narrated by Orson Welles, Gogol’s “The Nose,” and Mussorgsky’s Night on Bald Mountain.

title: Detroit Could Block Billionaire-Owned Concrete Plant From Further Neighborhood Expansion
content:
After years of community opposition, Detroit city officials have taken steps to stop a concrete mixing facility from further expanding into a residential neighborhood.

City Council members, acting on a recommendation last week from planning officials, will soon consider a rezoning measure that would restrict industrial activity at the site of the Kronos concrete plant and surrounding area. The concrete facility at its current size could stay and continue to operate as normal.

The planning recommendation comes after a BridgeDetroit and ProPublica investigation this year revealed how city officials helped Crown Enterprises, a real estate company owned by Detroit’s wealthy Moroun family, obtain property in Cadillac Heights and then provided latitude when its Kronos facility violated environmental laws. Residents have been filing complaints and protesting Kronos for years, frustrated by the dust, noise and other issues created by the concrete operation.

title: Digital Independence Day: Getting started with web analytics
content:
The holidays are behind us again, so it’s time to take a look at how your website has performed over the past month. Chances are you’ll be diving into the latest Google Analytics reports to do that.

Google Analytics has been the standard tool for web analytics for years. Because Google offers the tool for free to most people, it has become deeply rooted in the web. Around 83% of websites that track statistics do so with Google Analytics (that’s almost 48% of all websites). An incredible market share, then.

What many people (apparently) don’t realise is that by installing Google Analytics on their website, they’re handing their visitors’ browsing data to Google on a silver platter. And although you can strip down the tracker considerably so that it sends as little personal data as possible (which keeps you just within the GDPR rules, without having to ask for consent), you’re still giving Google a huge advantage in learning as much as possible about visitors and their behaviour.

So it’s time to break that monopoly and get started with the alternatives.

title: Von der Leyen touts ‘associate member’ status for Canada over objections of EU capitals
content:
MONTREAL, Canada — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Thursday she aims to bring EU-Canada relations to the “highest level possible,” touting potential associate member status in the bloc for Ottawa despite capitals having rejected the term a day earlier.

Von der Leyen’s overture comes on the eve of a landmark EU-Canada summit in Montreal where she and Prime Minister Mark Carney are due to announce plans for deeper cooperation against a backdrop of rising autocracy globally and unpredictable relations with U.S. President Donald Trump.

“Canada cannot become a full-fledged member of the EU because of geography, but we both want to bring our relationship to the highest level possible,” von der Leyen said in a speech hosted by the C.D. Howe Institute. “This is why we are discussing the idea of Canada becoming the first associate member of the European Union.”

No sooner had von der Leyen finished speaking than German Chancellor Friedrich Merz issued a statement saying that the EU and Canada were establishing an “Alliance for the Future” — without mentioning the associate member status. Germany has led the opposition to using the term, according to EU diplomats.

title: What animal bones in Malawi teach us about the social lives of people long ago
content:
In the ancient past, when human communities were small and the only way to travel was by walking, what were the chances of meeting a stranger? And what would happen next?

We know that ancient people lived by foraging their food from wild plants and animals, but we know a lot less about their social lives. Would there be conflict as people defended territory? Or would they choose to share? Sometimes survival depends on choosing wisely between these options. Defending a territory has a cost, and it’s not always worth it.

To understand how ancient people interacted with one another, we can start by looking at the food they ate. When food resources are densely clustered in predictable ways, it makes sense to establish and maintain a territory around them. When resources are sparsely distributed, they are harder to defend.

title: Wessen Wissen zählt? Ein Festival zum Zusammenbringen, Diskutieren und Feiern marginalisierten Wissens
content:
Wer etwas im Internet nachschlagen will, stößt früher oder später auf Wikipedia, entweder direkt oder über Suchmaschinen und KI-Anwendungen. Die größte freie Wissenssammlung der Welt bietet mit über 67 Millionen Artikeln einen umfangreichen Überblick über unzählige Themen. Doch es gibt noch Lücken: Manche Perspektiven und Erfahrungen sind bislang weniger sichtbar, etwa die Erinnerungen von Gastarbeiter*innenfamilien, die Geschichte des Widerstands gegen Rassismus oder das Wissen indigener Communitys. Vieles davon wurde bisher kaum in Büchern oder Archiven festgehalten und ist deshalb auch in Wikipedia noch nicht ausreichend vertreten.

Marginalisiertes Wissen ist das Wissen von Menschen und Gruppen, die gesellschaftlich an den Rand gedrängt werden, etwa weil sie Rassismus erfahren. Mit dem Programm re·shape hat Wikimedia Deutschland drei Jahre lang Menschen unterstützt, genau dieses Wissen selbst sichtbar zu machen.

content: Having a bad week? Kylian Mbappé might be having a worse one. On Monday, the French football star lost the Ballon d’Or, football's most prestigious individual award, to England's Harry Kane. And before he'd even had time to get over that, he's now in trouble with an entire country: China. It all started when a short clip from a French interview, aired six months ago, suddenly went viral at the start of the week. Asked about his favourite meme featuring himself, Mbappé said: “The one that made me laugh the most was the video where they put my face on some guy – I think he's a Chinese dictator.” For context, Mbappé has long been the subject of “dictator” jokes online. Even his teammates have joined in: French player Ousmane Dembélé has been heard calling him “Mobut” – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the former dictator of Zaire. title: Manifestos, Fear, and ‘Loser Thinking’: Inside Proton’s AI Reckoning
content:
Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, had a message for an employee in the company’s security Slack channel who urged the company to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August. “Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.”

In a follow-up message, Yen reiterated his point: “only losers think like that.” His ultimate message for the team was to “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.”

That exchange was just one of many that showed how Yen and other company executives are aggressively pushing Proton towards AI. Proton is a Swiss company that famously makes the encrypted email service Proton Mail and a suite of privacy and security-focused products, including an encrypted drive service, an authenticator app, a password manager, and more.

title: COP31 must amplify people power, not oil lobby voices
content:
The climate crisis is also a human rights crisis – claiming lives and turning life upside down for countless communities across the world.  

But while those profiting from fossil fuel expansion retain privileged access and influence over global climate negotiations, the people facing its harshest consequences, such as Indigenous Peoples or those living in climate-vulnerable communities, remain largely shut out of the decision-making. 

As directors of Amnesty International in Brazil, Türkiye and Australia, countries with a leading role in COP30 and COP31, we have seen how effective climate action depends on people being able to speak, organise, protest and participate. 

Last year in Belém, fossil fuel lobbyists outnumbered every national delegation except Brazil’s, exposing the imbalance of power within climate negotiations. COP31 should confront corporate capture and expand public participation. Instead, serious concerns have been raised over whether civil society will be able to speak freely and safely in Türkiye. 

Yet, the human rights needed to confront this crisis and demand justice are being eroded.
snippet: The climate crisis is also a human rights crisis – claiming lives and turning life upside down for countless communities across the world.

title: Ending China’s 60-Year Grip on Critical Minerals
content:
This is part of a series examining the central importance of critical minerals and the race to ensure Western supply.

Over decades, many democratic governments stopped planning strategically or placed losing bets on what future threats might be. They allowed the free market to outsource manufacturing and critical supply chains, including for the vital mineral inputs at the heart of every aspect of modern technology, from cell phones to power grids and F-35 fighter jets.

In contrast, Chinese leaders did not let markets get in the way. For six decades, Beijing has backed mineral mining and processing with state planning, cheap capital, and a tolerance for environmental costs that Western producers could not match.

It then consolidated the industry into state-controlled champions. Washington and Brussels now face the question Beijing answered long ago: when the market cannot price security, will government pay for it?

title: Andres Kasekamp: No more rules: The end of the transatlantic alliance?
content: The Transatlantic relationship relies on the rules-based international order established by the US and Western Allies after the Second World War. Rules, however, no longer apply to the behaviour of the United States under President Trump. His approach is purely transactional, and he does not believe in mutually beneficial alliances. He thinks that Europe and Canada have been ‘ripping off’ the US and now must pay for it. His administration is systematically neutering international bodies, for example by sanctioning judges of the International Criminal Court. Former Estonian President Lennart Meri quipped that international law is the nuclear weapon of small states. Trump, however, is returning the world to the law of jungle where weaker countries are vulnerable to larger predators.

title: Journalistiliitto: ”STT:n alasajo tulee kaatamaan myös muita tiedotusvälineitä”
content:
Suomen Tietotoimiston STT:n uutis- ja kuvaliiketoiminta päättyy maaliskuussa. Uutistoimisto aloitti kuukausi sitten muutosneuvottelut, jotka päättyivät keskiviikkona.

Muutosneuvotteluiden piirissä oli 95 vakituisessa työsuhteessa olevaa työntekijää. Tämänhetkisen arvion mukaan 89 henkilön työtehtävä päättyy. Lisäksi 30 ihmisen määräaikainen työsuhde tai puitesopimus päättyy.

Journalistiliiton puheenjohtajan Marjaana Varmavuoren mukaan uutinen on musertava.

– STT ei ole vain yksi mediayhtiö muiden joukossa. Sen rooli suomalaisessa luotettavan tiedon tuottamisessa ja jakelussa on korvaamaton. Olen syvästi järkyttynyt siitä, että valtio ja mediayhtiöt aikovat antaa kansallisen uutistoimistomme kaatua, Varmavuori sanoo tiedotteessa.

STT perustettiin vuonna 1887. Uutistoimiston alasajo heikentää Varmavuoren mukaan uutistarjontaa väistämättä.

– STT:n alasajo tulee kaatamaan myös muita tiedotusvälineitä. Valtiolla on vielä mahdollisuus pelastaa kansallinen uutistoimisto, mutta viimeinen hetki toimia on nyt. Meillä ei ole kerta kaikkiaan varaa joutua tilanteeseen, jossa ihmisten mahdollisuudet saada luotettavaa tietoa riippuvat siitä, missä he asuvat.

title: Africa Restitution Knowledge: Quality, Research and Discovery
content:
Have you ever created an article, but there were not enough sources to improve it, left it for a while, then months later found exactly the kind of resources you had been looking for? Yes, that was me with Ngonnso.

The Africa Restitution Knowledge Project focused on improving public knowledge about African restitution efforts through high-quality contributions to Wikipedia and Wikidata. It began when Olubusola Afolabi, the Community Engagement Lead at Free Knowledge Africa (FKA), reached out and mentioned that the project was in partnership with Open Restitution Africa (ORA). I knew that name sounded familiar. I went back to look at my contributions history and voila! I found out that while creating articles about individuals working on reparations, I had also created articles connected to ORA, restitution, the Ngonnso statue, and some of the African cultural objects that need to be returned. It was an easy YES.

title: Romania’s New Government: A Prime Minister in the Shadow of the PSD
content:
After nearly six months of political turmoil, Romania has had a new government since Tuesday, one dominated by the Social Democrats (PSD), who hold 12 of the 18 ministerial posts. At its head is an independent prime minister who appears to have few levers of power at his disposal.

Caught between pressure to rein in the budget deficit and the PSD’s grip on the Cabinet, new Prime Minister Luca Niculescu faces an uphill economic battle and has precious little room for political manoeuvre.

The new government takes office against a backdrop of economic hardship and deepening social polarisation. Niculescu secured parliamentary backing with the president’s threat of snap elections hanging over the vote. Yet the key portfolios remain firmly in Social Democratic hands, with one notable exception: the Finance Ministry, where Alexandru Nazare remains in post.

Aged 55, Niculescu, a former journalist and ambassador to France, faces the unenviable task of navigating two crises at once: an economy under mounting fiscal pressure and a Cabinet in which he appears to have little real authority over the PSD ministers.

title: What the new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy means for workers – and what’s next for implementation
content:
In June 2026, the International Labour Organisation (ILO) adopted a new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy. Following in the footsteps of the EU’s Platform Work Directive, this Convention extends data protection rights for platform workers and contains innovative provisions to protect against the adverse effects of automated decision-making globally. But this is only the beginning. In this article, EDRi member Privacy International explores what’s next for ratification, implementation and the future of regulating worker surveillance in the EU and around the world.

title: Tehran Revolutionary Court Sentences Three More Detainees from January Protests to Death
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Amirreza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and a cleric named Mehdi (surname unknown) were sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Among the charges brought against the three individuals in this case is allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel. The death sentences were communicated to them in prison on Monday, October 26, 2026.

Mehdi, another defendant in the case, is a cleric and a former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He has also been sentenced to death by the Special Clerical Court in a separate case on charges of “apostasy.” Consequently, two death sentences have been issued against him in two separate cases.

The three individuals were arrested separately by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026.

On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, they were transferred from the Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

title: UN Finds Age-Based Persecution of Palestinian Children
content:
A UN Commission of Inquiry concluded on October 14 that Israeli authorities have committed the crime against humanity of persecution against Palestinian children. Their findings recognize an important dimension that has not been given enough attention: children in the West Bank have been deliberately targeted—not just because of their nationality, race or ethnicity but also due to their age—in attacks causing serious bodily and mental harm. 

After making the same determination about Gaza in June, the commission expanded its finding to the West Bank, explaining: “the harm inflicted on children is not incidental or collateral to the broader violence affecting civilian population, but forms part of a pattern of intentional violence.” 

Age-based persecution is not limited to Gaza or the West Bank. Last November, judges at the International Criminal Court confirmed 39 charges, albeit in absentia, against Joseph Kony, leader of the Lord’s Resistance Army, for crimes in northern Uganda including persecution on age grounds.
