title: Revealed: UK relied on £2bn of ‘questionable accounting’ to hit its climate-aid goal
content:
• ‘Moving the goalposts’
  • ‘£1bn shortfall’
  • Accounting changes
  • Methodology

    • The UK has beaten its target to provide £11.6bn of climate aid to developing countries by 2026 – but only through “questionable accounting”. 

    As part of its obligations under the Paris Agreement, the UK pledged to give at least £11.6bn in overseas “climate finance” between 2021 and 2026.

    Now, Carbon Brief analysis reveals that around £2.1bn of the funds the UK counted towards this goal did not come from new spending.

    Instead, the government relabelled existing funding for development banks, private-sector investment and aid for Afghanistan, Sudan and other war-torn nations as “climate finance”.

    Without these changes, the UK would have fallen nearly £1bn short of its target.

    Carbon Brief’s analysis is based on numerous FOI requests and reveals the otherwise-unpublished details of the UK’s climate-finance spending.

    Experts and MPs say the use of “questionable” accounting shows the UK is “cutting corners” to hit its climate goals, while making unprecedented cuts to its foreign aid budget.

title: Rebuilding Ukraine: A Testing Ground for Western Innovation?
content:
Missiles rain down over Ukraine’s cities. Drones devastate the expanding battlefield. Although reconstruction may seem far off, the West needs to prepare for gigantic infrastructure projects, estimated to cost at least $590 billion over a decade. And that’s without counting additional devastation.

It will be a giant challenge for a labor-starved, financially strapped, war-torn country. But Ukraine’s needs could become a giant opportunity — provided that the country leverages artificial intelligence, robots, and drones.

The obstacles start with personnel. After widespread emigration and war deaths, Ukraine has only about half of the skilled construction workers it needs for reconstruction, a shortfall of up to 800,000 workers. Russia is deliberately destroying Ukraine’s production capacity: recent strikes shut down the country’s two largest steel mills, causing steel production to fall by more than half.

title: AI is stealing news readers: “We can’t live on a mission alone”
content:
A journalist checks facts, interviews experts and examines documents. Producing a good news story takes hours, sometimes days. Yet readers may never make it to the publisher’s website. Instead, they see an AI-generated summary or a story selected by a social media algorithm — often with no link back to the original publication. For publishers, that means fewer visits and growing dependence on technology companies.

It is a challenge we face in our own newsroom, too. The scale of the shift is illustrated by a Pew Research Center study. Google users who were shown an AI-generated summary clicked on a conventional search result in just 8% of visits. When no AI summary appeared, that figure rose to 15%. And links embedded in the AI summaries themselves? Users clicked on those in just 1% of visits.

“If we don’t want to be manipulated, we shouldn’t leave algorithms entirely under the control of Big Tech,” Katarzyna Szymielewicz, president of the Panoptykon Foundation, tells FocusEurope.pl.

title: Court Should Curb Abuse of Grand Jury Subpoenas Targeting Social Media Users
content:
A federal appeals court should curb the government’s abuse of grand jury subpoenas to unmask social media users who criticize lawless immigration enforcement.

That is the message from the ACLU, EFF, and other civil liberties and trade groups who filed a friend-of-the-court brief in a sealed case in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia.

The case involves the government’s investigation of an anonymous Reddit user who commented on a post about an immigration officer in Minnesota. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) first issued an administrative subpoena to Reddit to unmask the user. When the user challenged the subpoena in court on free speech and statutory grounds (as many others have), DHS withdrew it. But then the government obtained a separate grand jury subpoena—a subpoena issued by a prosecutor to gather evidence to present to a grand jury before any criminal charges are filed—for much of the same information. The user then challenged the grand jury subpoena too, and the case is currently being appealed.

title: Building bridges to adulthood: PA Education shares School to Work experience in Brussels
content:
How can local and regional actors provide more coordinated support to vulnerable young people as they move into adulthood? This question was at the centre of a workshop held on 14 October 2026 during the European Week of Regions and Cities in Brussels.

The workshop, No child left behind: building bridges to adulthood, was organised by the European Commission, Directorate-General for Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion (DG EMPL), together with Eurocities. Around 50 participants gathered to discuss how young people can receive more continuous and coordinated support when transitioning between education, employment and social services.

Anders Bergström, Policy Area Coordinator for Education under the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR), participated as a panellist, sharing experiences from the flagship School to Work (S2W).

title: No peace in Lebanon without strong allies
content:
It came as little surprise that Lebanon once again became a battleground in the regional war between Israel and Iran. Even without Hezbollah’s half-hearted rocket fire, Israel would have invaded the South again. No one knows the business of preventive war better than Tel Aviv. While Iran, under attack, has fared far better in the Gulf than initially expected, Israel has largely succeeded in imposing its agenda in Lebanon. Yet this is unlikely to bring Lebanon any peace. Instead, the country risks jumping out of the frying pan and into the fire: Iranian hegemony is simply being replaced by Israeli hegemony.

Lebanon’s reformist government, of course, frames things differently. Sovereignty is its watchword. The fact that Lebanon is negotiating directly with the Israeli state under US auspices is presented as an expression of that sovereignty. This, however, is an excessively optimistic assumption – one that misreads both Israel’s new security doctrine and the region’s emerging alignments. These separate negotiations will not bring stability. Instead, they will ensure that Lebanon remains divided, weak and occupied.

title: OPINION: Ending Nuclear Weapons
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 28 October 2026 (IDN) — Moscow and Washington urgently need to resume talks on a new framework for controlling nuclear weapons, said Dmitry Peskov, the Kremlin’s spokesman, on 20 October. “The absence of a treaty-based framework is creating a very dangerous situation”, he said.

Indeed, there has been no progress since 2010, when The New START Treaty, capped each side at 1,550 deployed weapons. This was a step forward—as recently as 2013, the total on both sides was 6,400. The treaty expired in February 2026. President Donald Trump did not want to extend it.

Fading ever more into the background as a popular issue is the possession of nuclear weapons. Once upon a time, there were regular marches down the streets all over the industrialised world. In the US, the nuclear freeze movement of the 1980s was an important factor in pushing President Ronald Reagan to reach out to Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev with a proposal to abolish all nuclear weapons. It didn’t happen, but there was significant progress on nuclear arms reduction, sometimes at a price.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil After Election Defeat and Amid Fraud Probes
content:
Just three days after securing more than 59 million votes in a fiercely contested presidential runoff, Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil on Tuesday and landed in the United States, halting investigations at home over his alleged ties to a banker accused of financial fraud.

A senior U.S. State Department official confirmed Tuesday that the U.S. "State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States."

Argentina's National Directorate of Migration (DNM) confirmed on the social network X that Flávio—son of the convicted former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro—crossed into Argentina through the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects the Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu with Argentina’s city of Puerto Iguazú.

Accompanied by his wife and two daughters, Bolsonaro then boarded a private jet that made a short stop in Ecuador before landing in Miami, Florida.

title: The Vibrant Color Wheels Designed by Goethe, Newton & Other Theorists of Color (1665–1810)
content:
Maybe it’s the cloistered headiness of Rene Descartes, or the rigorous austerity of Isaac Newton; maybe it’s all the leathern breeches, gray waistcoats, sallow faces, and powdered wigs… but we tend not to associate Enlightenment Europe with an explosion of color theory. Yet philosophers of the late 17th and 18th centuries were obsessed with light and sight. Descartes wrote a treatise on optics, as did Newton.

Newton first described in his 1672 paper the “revolutionary new theory of light and colour,” the University of Cambridge Whipple Library writes, “in which he claimed that experiments with prisms proved that white light was comprised of light of seven distinct colours.” Scientists debated Newton’s theory “well into the 19th century.”

One early opponent famously illustrated his rebuttal. Poet, writer, and scientist Johann Wolfgang von Goethe published Theory of Colors (see here), with its carefully hand-drawn and colored diagrams and wheels, in 1810. From Newton’s time onward, color theorists elaborated prevailing concepts with color wheels, the first attributed to Newton in 1704 (and drawn in black and white, above).

title: Online Event: “Europa in der Datenfalle – Warum es mehr digitale Souveränität bei Webdaten braucht”
content:
Anyone searching the web almost always uses a non-European search engine. Anyone training AI systems needs web data – and here, too, large corporations from the U.S. and China dominate. Europe is currently heavily dependent on overseas servies within the digital sector. This is not only an economic problem but also poses a threat to European values and the democratic order.

That is why we keep asking some urgent questions:

  • Why is web data so important for the (digital) economy?
  • What opportunities does a European web data infrastructure offer – both economically and socially?
  • And what specific steps must Germany and Europe take now?

    • We provide answers in our paper commissioned by the Heinrich Böll Foundation, “Why We Need More Digital Sovereignty Over Web Data,” which will be published in German on boell.de on November 23.
    We will discuss these findings on November 24 in the following panel set-up:

  • Dr. Stefan Voigt, co-founder and board member of the Open Search Foundation e.V., co-author of the study
  • Maike Scholz, Group Compliance, Head of the “Digital Ethics” Squad, Deutsche Telekom AG

title: How Cleta Mitchell Turned Trump’s “Big Lie” Into a Movement
content:
In July, not long before President Donald Trump delivered a primetime address questioning the legitimacy of American elections, the pioneering conservative election lawyer Cleta Mitchell and about two dozen of her associates logged onto a private video briefing with the White House.

Mitchell, who holds no formal position in the Trump administration, had been pivotal to Trump’s bid to challenge his loss in 2020, spearheading efforts to prove his claims of fraud and reverse his defeat in court.

After Joe Biden took office, when others abandoned the fight or scoffed as Trump clung to conspiracy theories, Mitchell doubled down, founding a grassroots organization devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Members of her group, the Election Integrity Network, were named to vital election-related positions in swing states and, later, in the second Trump administration.

The pre-speech briefing was an acknowledgment of just how consequential Mitchell and her organization had become. The White House had held similar sessions for key political players, such as governors, members of Congress and major press outlets.

title: EU lawmakers slam new border force powers to surveil social media
content:
BRUSSELS — New powers proposed for the EU’s border police Frontex to monitor social media pose a threat to free speech, European lawmakers and civil society groups have told POLITICO.

The EU Commission’s proposal Tuesday for a major revamp of the coast and border patrol agency included a broad and explicit mandate to monitor social media for information that aids or encourages illegal border crossings into the European Union.

Social democratic Italian lawmaker Brando Benifei told POLITICO it was “legitimate” for authorities to remove online advertisements for human smuggling: “But a broad social media surveillance mandate goes much further, placing online speech under a border agency’s watch.”

After a 2019 monitoring tender with similar powers was revoked over criticism about privacy violations, Benifei said “the Commission now proposes copying ICE’s invasive online tracking,” referencing the much-criticized surveillance tactics of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency.

title: Eurovision 2027: Is Canada singing its way into the European Union?
content:
Officials are meeting this week for the 21st Canada-European Union Leaders’ summit.

It comes only a month after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered Canada associate membership. A draft statement from Montréal, where Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, von der Leyen and EU Council President António Costa met for two days to discuss strengthening ties, calls for an “ever closer association” that will result “in a more active foreign and security policy partnership.”

The talks follow a series of milestones in the relationship between the transatlantic partners, including the announcement in July that Canada was joining the Eurovision song contest. It’s the first country to do so since Australia entered in 2015.

Eurovision is held every year in May, with member countries submitting one original song. Over the years, the event’s format has changed from an exclusive jury vote to a viewer televote and today’s combination of both.

Sometimes, voting can become political, with viewers voting according to their geopolitical preferences or diaspora communities casting ballots for their former home countries regardless of the quality of the performance.

title: EU’s new Arctic strategy signals shift in its geopolitical mindset
content:
The EU recently presented its latest Arctic strategy. It is the bloc’s fifth such strategy since 2008 and the first to be published since 2021, a few months before Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

This conflict has disrupted Arctic governance. The work of the Arctic Council, which includes Russia as one of its eight member states, was paused shortly after the invasion. The council is the primary forum for cooperation in the region.

Since 2022, the Russian security threat in the Arctic has also grown. Russia has engaged in hybrid activities in the region, ranging from disinformation operations and GPS jamming to the targeting of pipelines and undersea cables.

The EU’s new strategy has four priorities: strengthening peace, security and resilience in the Arctic, addressing climate change, delivering economic development and ensuring regional and social development for Arctic communities.

These priorities are broadly in line with the previous 2021 strategy, in which geopolitical issues were already more present than in earlier years. But there are several major changes.

title: Tutkimus: Tekoälylle juttelevat kokevat vähemmän stressiä kuin kirjoittamalla käyttävät
content:
Tekoälyn käyttö työpaikoilla ei muuta vain sitä, mitä työntekijät tekevät, vaan myös tapaa, jolla teknologiaa käytetään. Kirjoitettujen kehotteiden rinnalla tekoälyn kanssa keskustellaan yhä enemmän puhumalla.

Jabra Research Instituten WorkLife 2026: The New Shape of Work -raporttia varten haastateltiin yli 6 000 tietotyöläistä Saksassa, Yhdysvalloissa, Isossa-Britanniassa, Ranskassa, Puolassa ja Intiassa. Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin muun muassa sitä, miten erilaiset tekoälyn käyttötavat liittyvät työntekijöiden kokemuksiin työstä ja hyvinvoinnista.

Tekoälylle säännöllisesti puhuvat raportoivat 24 prosenttia harvemmin stressistä ja 23 prosenttia harvemmin uupumuksesta kuin tekoälyä vain kirjoittamalla käyttävät. Lisäksi he kertovat 37 prosenttia useammin kokevansa työnsä turvatuksi.

Tulokset kertovat ryhmien välisestä yhteydestä, eivät siitä, että tekoälylle puhuminen itsessään vähentäisi stressiä tai uupumusta.

title: Fünf gute Gründe, für Wikipedia zu spenden
content:
Die Wikipedia-Spendenkampagne 2026 ist gestartet. In den kommenden Wochen rufen wir die Menschen in Deutschland auf, die freie Online-Enzyklopädie und ihre ehrenamtliche Community zu unterstützen. Das Spendenziel liegt bei 8,4 Millionen Euro.

Hier kommen fünf gute Gründe, für Wikipedia zu spenden.

„Es gibt doch jetzt KI – warum sollte ich noch für Wikipedia spenden?“ Diese Frage haben sich vielleicht schon einige gestellt. Die Antwort ist einfach: Wer möchte, dass die Antwort des eigenen Chatbots halbwegs stimmt, sollte für Wikipedia spenden. KI-Systeme und intelligente Suchmaschinen greifen Informationen im gesamten Netz ab – Wikipedia ist dabei eine der wichtigsten Grundlagen. Denn hier gibt es über 67 Millionen sorgfältig recherchierte Artikel mit nachvollziehbaren Quellen und eine engagierte Community, die das Wissen gemeinsam überprüft und ständig verbessert.

title: Loans don't grow on trees
content: Ever wondered what tobacco and banks have in common? Very soon, both will be warning consumers about the risks associated with their products. From 20 November, under new EU rules, adverts for consumer credit will have to include a clear and prominent warning: “Caution! Borrowing money costs money.” Very similar to the ones you see on cigarette packets. The requirement to warn consumers that loans don't grow on trees is part of new regulation to protect EU consumers taking out loans. Lenders will also face stricter requirements on the information they provide in credit adverts. This includes the total cost of borrowing and, where applicable, the loan's duration and repayment instalments. Misleading advertising will also be prohibited. The updated rules extend consumer credit protections to small loans of less than €200 and “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) schemes, which have become increasingly common in online shopping. There is one exception, though: shops that offer interest-free credit directly, without involving a third-party such as Klarna, as long as the purchase is repaid within 50 days. title: Tanzania: Authorities weaponize counterterrorism laws to restrict civic space amid pervasive impunity over violent election crackdown
content:
Tanzanian authorities have failed to hold anyone accountable for the violence security forces inflicted on protesters, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured in the wake of the 2025 general election, Amnesty International said on the first anniversary of the crackdown.

Instead of delivering justice and accountability, authorities have withheld a Commission of Inquiry report from the public and intensified attacks on civic space through the abuse of counterterrorism laws.

Not a single official has been criminally investigated, let alone prosecuted and punished for the excessive force that Tanzanian security forces used against protesters. In fact, the situation has only deteriorated since the crackdown began. In a classic tactic pulled out of the authoritarian playbook, the authorities are increasingly weaponizing counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear,”

Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa

title: Analysis: How the UK spent more than £11.6bn on climate aid since 2021
content:
• The UK has supported around 500 climate projects since 2021
  • UK climate aid has reached record levels – but is set to drop
  • Afghanistan received more bilateral climate aid than any other country
  • Development banks and private-sector funders are among the biggest beneficiaries
  • Methodology

    • The UK has spent £12.8bn on climate aid for developing countries since 2021, according to official figures obtained by Carbon Brief.

    Freedom-of-information (FOI) requests reveal how the UK has used its “climate finance” to support everything from solar projects in Mozambique to carbon offsets in the Amazon.

    UK climate funding, which reached a record £4bn this year, has supported roughly 500 aid projects, climate funds and private-investment initiatives over the past five years.

    With this spending, the UK has surpassed its £11.6bn climate-finance target for this period, although Carbon Brief analysis shows that it has partly relied on “questionable accounting”.

    This target is part of the UK’s ongoing responsibility under UN climate treaties to financially support developing countries in their efforts to tackle climate change.

title: EU Tech Rules Pit Privacy Against Competition
content:
After running two half marathons, I decided to get serious and buy a sports watch. As an iPhone owner, I wanted to know if a watch from another manufacturer would work well with my phone. 

That simple question exposes a crucial tension in European tech policy. On the one hand, Europeans pride themselves on producing the world’s most powerful digital privacy rules, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). On the other hand, they pride themselves on producing the world’s most powerful rules around sharing data. The Digital Markets Act (DMA) requires Apple and other “gatekeepers” to open their devices to competing products in the name of consumer choice and market competitiveness.  

But there’s a giant problem: the two sets of rules often fight with each other.

title: How Romania Is Defending the Black Sea as Russian Attacks Threaten Shipping
content:
Russian drone attacks on commercial vessels have intensified, with at least seven ships targeted in the western Black Sea, near Romania and Bulgaria, in the first half of October alone.

Reuters reported on 15 October that at least 23 seafarers had been killed or were missing following attacks on the vessels.

The attacks pose a serious threat to regional security and have prompted Romania and Bulgaria to call on NATO to strengthen its defences along the alliance’s eastern flank.

Romania’s Black Sea defences currently rely on the Romanian Naval Forces, supported by the Air Force and NATO allies, against a backdrop of mounting regional tensions.

The new Contraamiral August Roman corvette: Commissioned into service in the summer of 2026, the vessel, acquired from Turkey and belonging to the Hisar class, is currently the Romanian Navy’s most modern ship. It is now being fitted with the country’s first state-of-the-art Naval Strike Missile (NSM) anti-ship systems, recently delivered to Romania.

EFF and other groups are fighting back. In our latest EFFector newsletter, we're talking about a recent victory in our lawsuit against the government for sharing federal workers' confidential personnel files with DOGE.

title: Youth Democracy Festivals empower youth as the future of democracy
content:
Through D-Effect project, young people across the Baltic Sea Region co-create Youth Democracy Festivals, strengthening civic participation, democratic skills and cooperation between youth and decision-makers.

Young people are often invited to discuss democracy, but rarely have a real opportunity to shape it. The Interreg South Baltic project D-Effect is changing this approach by giving youth an active role in designing and delivering democratic initiatives within their communities.

Implemented by partners from Poland, Sweden, Denmark, Germany and Lithuania, D-Effect promotes civic engagement through a practical methodology built around Round Tables, Youth Democracy Festivals (YDF) and direct dialogue with decision-makers. Rather than being passive participants, young people become co-creators of activities that address local challenges and strengthen democratic culture.

title: Alarming Attacks on Women Politicians
content:
Overwhelmed by threats—and fearing for her personal safety Satya Rhodes-Conway the current mayor of Madison, Wisconsin in the US, announced on October 23 that she was dropping her bid for reelection. "The price of being in public office has gotten too high,” she said.

Globally, women in public life face alarming levels of political violence, including tech-facilitated sexual and gender-based violence, with little protection or recourse. While research finds chillingly high rates of violence against both women and men in politics, women are at greater risk and face more sexualized and gendered violence.

title: China Sentences Ex Anti-Graft Official to Suspended Death for Bribery
content:
A Chinese court sentenced a former senior anti-graft official at the China ​Securities Regulatory Commission, to a suspended death sentence for accepting more than 436 million yuan ($65.4 million) in bribes.

Between 1998 and 2025, Wang Huimin abused his positions in the northwestern Xinjiang region and at the national securities regulator to secure business and fundraising favors for companies and individuals in exchange for the illicit payments, the state-run Xinhua news agency reported.

A suspended death sentence gives the 67-year-old Wang Huimin a two-year reprieve from execution, after which the penalty is automatically commuted to life in prison under Chinese law.

title: EU scraps ‘associate member’ offer for Canada
content:
BRUSSELS — EU countries have dropped the idea of offering Canada “associate member” status in the 27-member bloc, opting instead for softer language promising “ever closer association” ahead of a landmark EU-Canada summit, according to the latest version of the draft statement, seen by POLITICO.

A group of countries including Germany, Greece and France all objected to mentioning associate membership in a joint EU-Canada statement to be issued in Montreal, the diplomats said.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen had originally proposed “associate membership” for Canada in her State of the European Union speech in September, catching some EU countries off-guard.

A previous draft of the joint statement had read that the EU and Canada would “work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada Summit the concept of Associate Member that will reflect, through this even closer association, our common endeavour and cooperation towards our shared goals of prosperity, economic security and strategic autonomy.”

title: Social media is full of weird video game mashups. Where are they all coming from?
content:
AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games. Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from.

title: Barcelona unrest: how to fabricate a protest in the age of TikTok
content:
Imagine coming across a TikTok post calling you to protest for better public schools. You scan a QR code to get more information, and find yourself in a private chat where the instructions are not about education or political organising, but about looting.

This was the picture that emerged in Barcelona on October 24. Around 20 TikTok accounts linked to the anonymous Blocus platform had promoted gatherings across Spain, inviting young people to mobilise.

The public accounts echoed the French student movement and called for similar action in Plaça Catalunya, right next to the city’s housing rights encampment. Yet no evidence links the two movements – a fact that Barcelona’s mayor Jaume Collboni has explicitly acknowledged.

The gathering quickly descended into masked youths smashing shop windows and confronting the police. The night ended with 130 young people arrested, 76 of them underage, and 14 police officers injured.

The TikTok accounts that spurred these particular protests have since been deleted, along with all of their posts and content.

title: I’ve been talking to MAGA supporters for years, and here’s why some are sticking with Trump — and others are not
content:
President Donald Trump’s approval ratings are cratering. Even his Make America Great Again, or MAGA, diehards have reservations.

This fact was evident to me when I attended MAGA rallies in three states on Oct. 24-25, 2026. One was a Turning Point USA get-out-the-vote event outside Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.

Along with a few dozen America First stalwarts wearing white “America the Beautiful” caps, I sat on a wooden table under a small picnic pavilion listening to speakers such as MAGA activist Scott Presler and Trump-endorsed U.S. Rep. Dan Meuser. Meuser reeled off MAGA talking points, including the supposed threat posed by transgender athletes and bathroom use, immigrant voter fraud and the “billionaire anarchist George Soros.”

Remarkably, the speakers barely mentioned Trump. The audience clapped politely, but the energy was tepid compared to the many MAGA rallies I attended in 2024, when the Pennsylvania landscape was dotted with Trump and MAGA signs. This time I saw none.

The numbers bear out what I observed.

Base Auroran perustana ja markkinoinnin kärkinä ovat Oulun alueen olemassa olevat vahvuudet: kehittyneet testausympäristöt, kansainvälisesti korkeatasoinen tutkimus, innovatiiviset yritykset sekä pitkä kokemus teknologian kehittämisestä.

Base Aurora yhteisenä nimittäjänä luo uusia mahdollisuuksia yhteiskehittämiseen, todellisten käyttöympäristöjen testaukseen, demonstraatioihin ja validointiin erityisesti puolustus- ja kaksoiskäyttöteknologioissa.

Oulusta käynnistyvän kokonaisuuden tavoitteena on vahvistaa yritysten, tutkimusorganisaatioiden ja puolustussektorin välistä yhteistyötä, parantaa testauskyvykkyyksien saavutettavuutta sekä tukea kansainvälistä teknologiakehitystä.

title: Suomen luonnon tulevaisuus on omissa käsissämme: Elinympäristöjen suojeleminen voittaa ilmastonmuutoksen torjunnan paikallistasolla
content:
Elinympäristöjen koostumus selittää useimpien eläinryhmien esiintymistä ja runsautta paremmin kuin ilmasto, selvisi vastoin ennakko-odotuksia uudesta tutkimuksesta. Tulos korostaa maankäytön suunnittelun merkitystä luonnon monimuotoisuuden turvaamisessa.

Tutkijat halusivat ymmärtää, kumpi määrittää lajien esiintymistä ja runsautta enemmän: ilmasto vai elinympäristöihin liittyvät tekijät, kuten alueen luonnontilaisuus ja ihmistoiminnan muokkaaman maan osuus. Vastaus ohjaa ratkaisevasti sitä, miten käynnissä olevaa luonnon monimuotoisuuden vähenemistä voidaan estää.

”Elinympäristöjen merkitys oli erityisen suuri perhosille, linnuille ja piennisäkkäille. Suurten nisäkkäiden ja yöperhosten kohdalla elinympäristöt ja ilmasto ovat suhteellisesti yhtä tärkeitä,” sanoo Nature Communicationsissa ilmestyneessä artikkelissa sen pääkirjoittaja Emy Guilbault Helsingin yliopiston tiedotteen mukaan.

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin 503 maalla elävää eläinlajia ja niiden esiintyvyydessä tapahtuneita muutoksia kahdenkymmenen vuoden aikana koko Suomessa ja sen kaikilla ilmastovyöhykkeillä. Yli kolmen miljoonan havainnon analysoimiseen tarvittiin nykyaikaisia tilastollisia menetelmiä.

title: How to shut down half a country in 10 days
content: Walking down the aisle of your local supermarket, and all you see are bare shelves and rows of empty boxes. A sign reads: “Delivery not received. Sorry for the inconvenience.” There is no bread, fruit, or vegetables – just frozen food, which you quickly stock up on. This is not a flashback to 2020, when panic-buying for pasta and toilet paper during the Covid-19 pandemic left supermarket shelves emptied. This time, the shortages are linked to workers' protests in southern Italy over soaring fuel prices. It all began with the farmers on 10 October: they called for mass demonstrations in the Italian regions of Calabria, Apulia, Basilicata, and Sicily, and workers in the transport sector immediately joined. Striking hauliers switched off their engines on roads and motorways, and refused to unload their goods. Fishermen also joined the protests, leaving their boats docked at port. The protesters' message is clear: running a farm, a transport or fishing business has become too expensive. Fuel is one major cost, but it's far from being the only one. title: Serbia’s New Government Needs New Security Services
content:
Now that Aleksandar Vučić’s government is gone, evicted by joyous voters, EU leaders will be wondering how to approach Serbia’s new administration.

What can the West offer? There will no doubt be many answers, but the best is to encourage root-and-branch reform of the country’s over-mighty and outdated security system.

The election victory changes the government and provides a strong political mandate, but it will not automatically affect the agencies at the heart of government. The state remains the same until the people, rules and assumptions in the intelligence services and the army change. That is why the first serious test of the new government will be the security sector, and not the distribution of ministries.

title: Knife Attacks in Polish Schools: What Drives Student Violence?
content:
Judging by international education assessments such as PISA, Poland appears to be a model of academic achievement. In three key areas — science, mathematics and reading comprehension — Polish 15-year-olds perform significantly above both the EU and OECD averages.

Within Europe, they are surpassed primarily by Estonia, and in certain subjects by Finland and Ireland. Yet behind these impressive results lies a deep fracture in the education system. The same research suggests that Polish students rank among the lowest in perseverance and motivation to learn. Nearly two-thirds of teenagers (63%) believe that school does little or nothing to prepare them for adult life, while 40% explicitly say that the time they spend in the classroom is wasted.

content:

October 28, 2025

Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

NARRATION

On the morning of October 28th, 2025, hundreds of police officers surrounded two low-income neighborhoods in Rio de Janeiro.

By nightfall, the operation would become the deadliest in Brazil's history.

122 people were killed, including two children and five police officers. According to the autopsy records, over eighty five percent of non-police victims were Black.

Police in Rio de Janeiro are required by Supreme Court order to wear body cameras. 

However, only twenty-three percent of officers wore body cameras that day, and in the footage reviewed by Human Rights Watch, not a single killing was captured on camera.

title: Jäänmurtajat jäämerellisen vallan symboleina Venäjällä ja Kanadassa
content: Tässä meristrategian teoriaperinteeseen kytkeytyvässä artikkelissa tarkastellaan viitteitä Venäjän ja Kanadan merellisestä vallasta Jäämerellä kulttuuristen teennösten eli artefaktien kautta. Tarkastelukehyksenä toimii Andrew Lambertin kehittelemä teoria, jonka mukaisesti valtion merellinen valta rakentuu sen merelliselle kulttuuri-identiteetille. Artikkelissa huomio kiinnitetään nimenomaisesti jäämerelliseen kulttuuri-identiteettiin, jota symboloivaksi tulkitaan polaarijäänmurtajaviittausten ilmentyminen kansallisessa kulttuurissa. Ilmentymien määrää ja merkitystä tarkastellaan viidessä kategoriassa: muistomerkit, musiikki, rahat, seremoniat ja postimerkit. Tarkastelusta käy ilmi, että Venäjällä kulttuurisissa teennöksissä viittauksia polaarijäänmurtajiin esiintyy selvästi Kanadaa enemmän. Lambertin teorian valossa Venäjällä olisi siis paremmat lähtökohdat merelliselle vallalle Jäämerellä. Kanadankin kulttuurissa kuitenkin on jäämerellisyyteen viittaavia piirteitä. Kanadalle olisi nykyisistä lähtökohdistaan verrattain helppo valita kehittää kulttuuriaan nykyistä jäämerellisemmäksi ja siten luoda edellytyksiä jäämerellisen valtansa kasvattamiselle.

title: Russian Billionaire Takes Tiny Norwegian News Outlet to Court in London
content:
Russian tycoon Vitaly Orlov is suing The Barents Observer, a small Norwegian news outlet, over its reporting on sanctions against his fishing company. 

The Barents Observer is a six-person non-profit newsroom in Kirkenes, a town of about 7,000 people in Norway’s far north. But the lawsuit isn’t taking place there — or even in Norway. Instead, Orlov has lodged a defamation suit in the High Court of London.

“We don’t even have money for plane tickets to go to the court,” said Editor in Chief Thomas Nilsen.

“It’s just not possible for us to defend ourselves against all of the claims,” he told OCCRP’s Norwegian media partner, NRK, adding that if Orlov is awarded some legal costs, The Barents Observer “will go bankrupt.” 

Orlov’s fishing company, Norebo JSC, said in a statement provided to OCCRP that the choice of London as a venue for the lawsuit was related to the fact that The Barents Observer publishes in English.

“The Barents Observer is a Norwegian publication that publishes in English and now complains at being sued in England. This is the very country The Barents Observer has courted,” the company said.

title: UK’s Healey cracks down on VAT-shirking online sellers
content:
LONDON — U.K. Chancellor John Healey has moved to crack down on a loophole exploited by overseas sellers to avoid paying VAT. 

“I will strengthen the requirements for online marketplaces so that sellers cannot avoid paying VAT when they sell online,” Healey said in Wednesday’s budget.

From October 2027, online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay and Temu will be responsible for collecting tax owed by all retailers with an annual turnover of more than £90,000 through a single marketplace.

Previously, these marketplaces only had to collect VAT on behalf of overseas sellers and not domestic ones. Some overseas sellers then exploited this gap to avoid paying the tax by registering as U.K. based companies.

The government plans to reinvest the savings made from this policy into the high street through reductions to business rates.

The government launched an eight-week consultation into extending VAT online marketplace liability in June, after mounting pressure from retailers. 

Amazon estimated that up to £3.2 billion of sales across online retailers in the U.K. are made by sellers avoiding VAT collection — costing the Treasury hundreds of millions each year in lost revenue.

title: Castle Walls review – Prime’s first fully AI-generated show is here, and it’s a Vaseline-smeared mess
content:
Billed as the first end-to-end AI-created series on a major streaming service, this Turkish show looks like the result of the prompt ‘make it cinematic’

Just as the world reels from Elon Musk’s AI-powered The Odyssey remake – though “remake” feels rather generous for a seven-minute splat of synthetic sludge – another bucket of AI gunk is dropped on to our faces. For Prime Video’s AI-generated TV series Castle Walls, produced by Turkish production studio Ay Yapım using a melange of generative video tools, has arrived, billed as the first end-to-end AI-created series to premiere on a major streaming platform.

It’s certainly more epic than Musk’s production, consisting of two 17-minute episodes. Set in the 11th century, the show revolves around the historic Alamut Castle, although it’s entirely absent of any real sense of time or place. I was briefly intrigued by the opening images, with their bold palette of blues and mustard browns and yellows – but as soon as the “people” appeared, looking like Vaseline-smeared Madame Tussauds creations slowly melting in the sun, everything came crashing down.
snippet: Billed as the first end-to-end AI-created series on a major streaming service, this Turkish show looks like the result of the prompt ‘make it cinematic’

title: Private equity is buying up more methadone clinics – access to the lifesaving drug isn’t getting easier
content:
Three times a week, Amber Titus wakes up at 5 a.m. to get ready for the 45-minute drive to the methadone clinic.

Titus, 38, and her husband live with their two young children in Bisbee Junction, Arizona, a rural community near the U.S.-Mexico border. The couple started taking methadone, a medication that treats opioid addiction, in early 2025.

“It’s been a godsend,” she said.

But accessing methadone is not easy. The closest place they can receive treatment is a clinic in Sierra Vista, about 30 miles from their home.

The clinic opens on weekdays at 4:30 a.m. but closes before midday. Titus has to get her methadone dose and arrive at work in Bisbee before her shift starts at 9 a.m.

Arriving just 10 to 15 minutes late for an appointment can mean missing a dose because rules are so strict, she said, even when the clinic is still open.

That’s the routine when they have their own transportation. In August, their car was totaled in a crash. Until they got another one, Titus called Medicaid, her insurance provider, to schedule rides to the clinic.

title: Less friendly with the rest of the world
content: European national football teams play fewer friendlies against non-European opponents than they used to. The number of friendly games played between a UEFA national team and a team from a different confederation dropped from an average of 55.3 games a year before 2019 to 38.6 after 2019. The drop coincides with the launch of the UEFA Nations League in late 2018. This new competition would replace many of the international friendlies teams used to play. UEFA said the aim was to add “status and appeal to national team football.” The number of intercontinental friendlies varies from year to year. It tends to rise in World Cup years, when teams seek opponents from other continents to prepare for the tournament. The number of friendlies rose in 2026, when 43 of the year’s 67 friendlies against non-European teams were played in June, just before the expanded World Cup kicked off.

title: ‘There is no inevitable dystopia’: Jeanette Winterson on AI and the future of humanity
content:
The author believes we are at a turning point as a species – and even in the shadow of big tech it’s up to us how we want to proceed

‘I am a storyteller by trade,” writes Jeanette Winterson on the first page of her 2021 book 12 Bytes, an idiosyncratic and thought-provoking series of essays in which she considered just how artificial intelligence might change everything about our lives. “And I know everything we do is a fiction until it’s a fact: the dream of flying, the dream of space travel, the dream of speaking to someone instantly, across time and space, the dream of not dying – or of returning.”

She had already been thinking about our possible futures for at least 15 years – her 2007 novel, The Stone Gods, for instance, imagined a post-climate catastrophe world populated by robots and humans who never age, while 12 Bytes was preceded by Frankisstein: A Love Story, which alternates a recreation of the summer Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein with a trans doctor’s travels among present-day cryogenecists and AI-enabled robots.

title: Medieval ghost stories featured rotten flesh, the walking dead and spoon-stealing spirits
content:
Stories of wandering spirits and the restless dead were common in the Middle Ages. These ghostly encounters were recorded in a wide variety of medieval literature.

Medieval ghost stories combined folklore traditions with religious doctrine. The widespread belief in purgatory – a place where souls were cleansed of sin before entering heaven – helped fuel the belief in ghosts.

Spirits of the departed were thought able to return, exhorting the living to pray for them and make amends on their behalf to aid their passage through purgatory. As a result, medieval ghost stories often contained a strong moral and religious message.

Historians have long been fascinated by a series of 12 ghost stories written down in the early years of the 15th century at Byland Abbey, a Cistercian monastery in north Yorkshire. They recorded a bizarre and eclectic array of ghosts, featuring shape-shifting spirits, miracle stories and the walking dead, who crept up on the living.

title: It's not the bots, Flock
content:
Flock CEO Garrett Langley says some interesting things to cops behind closed doors. He recently lied about his surveillance technology’s role in tracking a woman who had self-administered an abortion and 404 Media’s coverage of that incident, calling it “entirely false.” Now, in leaked audio obtained by 404 Media, Langley is saying the protests that have broken out around the country against his company, many of which have resulted in communities canceling their contracts with Flock and bagging up the cameras, are not real. Seems pretty real to me! 

Garrett Langley, the CEO of automatic license plate reader company Flock, told an audience of police chiefs at a private police conference Sunday that anti-Flock protests around the country are not real, according to leaked audio obtained by 404 Media.

He also said his wife advised him to never apologize, said he would prefer to never do interviews with the press again, and claimed without evidence that the social media opposition to Flock is driven mostly by Russian bots.

title: Russia: African leaders must use summit to call for an end to trafficking of Africans into Russian military
content:
African leaders attending the Russia-Africa summit must call on the Russian authorities to immediately end the coercive and deceptive recruitment of African nationals into Russia’s military forces to fight against Ukraine, Amnesty International’s African section directors said in an open letter ahead of the summit, which takes place from 28 to 29 October in Moscow.

“For African leaders to remain silent on this issue would be a profound disservice to the people of their countries. We urge them to address this issue directly with the Russian authorities at the Russia-Africa Summit 2026 and call on Russia to take immediate steps to end these practices, which in many cases amount to trafficking — a crime under international law,” said directors of Amnesty International’s sections across Africa.

“At a moment when many African governments are speaking up about the enduring legacy of colonialism, and the importance of sovereignty and African agency in international affairs, they must reject any practice that treats nationals of African countries as a commodity for other countries’ political and military objectives.”

title: Parlamentarisches Frühstück zum Informationsfreiheitsgesetz
content: Das Informationsfreiheitsgesetz (IFG) des Bundes besteht de facto seit 20 Jahren. Es hat den Zugang zu staatlichen Informationen erleichtert und damit neue Möglichkeiten für Bürger:innen, Journalist:innen, Wissenschaft, Zivilgesellschaft und Wirtschaft geschaffen, staatliches Handeln nachzuvollziehen und kritisch zu begleiten. Doch die aktuellen Pläne des Koalitionsausschusses stellen infrage, wie weit dieses Recht künftig noch reichen soll. Zu diesem Thema veranstaltete das Bündnis F5 am 9.10. sein dreizehntes parlamentarisches Frühstück, diesmal unter der gemeinsamen Schirmherrschaft drei Abgeordneter der SPD-Bundestagsfraktion: Johannes Schätzl, digitalpolitischer Sprecher, Carmen Wegge, rechtspolitische Sprecherin, und Sebastian Fiedler, innenpolitischer Sprecher.

title: Q&A: Why are UK energy bills so high – and how could they be lowered?
content:
• What is driving high energy bills?
  • What has been done to limit bills so far?
  • What options are there for bringing down bills?
  • Is there a ‘cheap power’ alternative if the UK slows down?
  • Can electrification of homes and businesses help cut bills?

    • Energy bills in the UK have continued to soar in 2026, with intense debate raging about how to bring them down. 

    In October 2026, the cap on household energy bills reached its highest level in three years, rising by £60 amid high gas prices driven by the Iran war.

    The cap is forecast to jump by as much as another quarter in January 2027, pushing annual energy bills towards £2,200.

    Energy bills have not been that high since 2022 when, in the fallout of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the UK government spent more than £60bn on supporting consumers through the crisis.

    While expensive gas is behind the lion’s share of the rise in bills since 2020, policy costs and investment in the gas and electricity grids are also putting some pressure on prices.

    This has sparked conflicting calls to continue the clean-energy transition to get off the “fossil-fuel rollercoaster”, to move more slowly – or to abandon climate goals in favour of more gas.

title: Morocco: Release detained Sahrawi activists and end reprisals against prisoners’ families
content:
CIVICUS calls on the Moroccan authorities to immediately release seven Sahrawi activists arrested during a peaceful gathering in Rabat on 12 October 2026 and to end reprisals against their families and supporters. The gathering was organised in support of Sahrawi prisoners from the Gdeim Izik group, who are on an open-ended hunger strike. Reports of ill-treatment in custody and restrictions on families and supporters seeking to attend court proceedings have heightened concerns about the activists’ safety, due process rights and freedom of peaceful assembly.

Police, supported by auxiliary forces, reportedly used physical force against participants outside the General Delegation for Prison Administration and Reintegration.They then arrested seven activists; Hassana Douihi, Salah Eddine Sabbar, Brahim Babit, Mohamed Mrabet, Khalid Boufriwa, El Houssein Chihab and Aziz El Ouahidi. Transliteration of some names varies across sources.

On 14 October, after about 48 hours in custody, the seven activists were brought before the public prosecutor. They reportedly face allegations including participation in an unauthorised gathering and violence against public security personnel.

title: Wanted: A Feminist UN Secretary-General for ‘We the Peoples’, Not the Powerful
content:
Notwithstanding last minute shenanigans and the possibility of backroom deals by powerful states, two women from Latin America are leading contenders in the race for the UN’s next Secretary-General. After 80-plus years of men-only leadership, momentum is building to break the glass ceiling at the global institution dedicated to saving future generations from the scourge of war.

Design flaws in the somewhat opaque appointment process that bestow arbitrary veto powers on the five permanent UN Security Council members could, however, torpedo the aspiration for equitable representation for women at the helm for the world body. But there is still time to build public pressure on governments to do the right thing by appointing a feminist woman leader from Latin America and the Caribbean in deference to the principle of regional rotation.

title: Commons Stories: Part 1
content:
by Molly Van Houweling
The serendipity and delight of connecting with fellow humans across time and space through acts of creativity and sharing.

by Vito Quaglia
To me, the commons means democracy. The commons nurtures the sharing of ideas, solutions, and creativity. It allows for information to be accessed by anyone and everyone. At its core, the commons is nondiscriminatory; it ensures that knowledge, art, and culture are enjoyed by an ecosystem that doesn’t depend on location, social capital, or economic status. Its main features are cooperation and cohabitation. At the current moment, the commons is vulnerable to rapid changes to its ecosystem. It is more important than ever that the commons foster the sharing of solutions that will ultimately save itself.

by Jocelyn Miyara
The commons is a collective and collaborative space where knowledge can be shared openly & freely. In today’s internet age, it is an important counterbalance to the increasingly commercial and controlled spaces in which information is shared. Open sharing is an antidote to that.

title: "Dark Day for Journalism": Egypt Shutters Independent News Site Mada Masr, Detains Editor
content:
A court in Cairo has ordered the closure of the independent Egyptian news site Mada Masr. The court also ordered the site’s editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, to be detained until she pays a fine of over $50,000. She was convicted on charges of managing an unlicensed website. Mada Masr is “the flagship independent media outlet in Egypt and a pillar of independent media in the region,” says Sharif Abdel Kouddous of Drop Site News, who previously worked at Mada Masr. The independent outlet was founded in 2013 “in the midst of Egypt’s revolution and counterrevolution” and has “managed to survive all of those years in one of the most hostile media environments” in the world. Still, “what happened today is an unprecedented escalation” because Attalah and Mada Masr had never before been referred to trial.

Kouddous adds that the attack on Mada Masr comes less than a month after Egyptian authorities arrested an entire newsroom at the independent fact-checking outlet Matsadaash. They remain behind bars.

title: MusicSphere releases new video on first Use Case
content:
On 2nd–3rd June 2026, the MusicSphere consortium gathered in Thessaloniki, Greece, for its first Use Case Meeting, hosted by the International Hellenic University (IHU) and LUTHIEROS. The visit brought partners closer to the rich heritage of ancient and modern pipe organs, with visits to the Greek Evangelical Church of Katerini, the Archaeological Museum of Dion, and the SEIKILO Museum of Ancient Music.

At the heart of the visit was the Hydraulis of Dion, an extraordinary ancient Greek water-powered organ and the focus of MusicSphere’s first use case. Partners explored its historical significance and the challenges of reconstructing an instrument that has survived only in fragments. Through 3D reconstruction, digital twins, acoustic modelling, artificial intelligence and immersive technologies, MusicSphere aims to bring this remarkable piece of musical heritage closer to researchers and the public, exploring how it may have looked, functioned and sounded in the ancient world. The second day focused on project progress, technical developments and collaboration, helping lay the foundations for the Hydraulis of Dion Digital Twin.

title: Social Media When Elections Are Close: Doing the Impossible Better
content:
Everyone knows, or should, that perfect (balanced, targeted, transparent, swift and swiftly appealable) content moderation at scale is impossible. That doesn’t mean powerful social platforms don’t have to try to get at least reasonably close, especially when access to good information can have a profound effect on political participation and speech.

That’s why so many people, including the Meta Oversight Board, criticized Meta for suspending a major political Instagram account for hours during a huge early voting push on October 17; and for allegedly boosting one candidate in Brazil’s recent presidential election. Meta denies deliberate interference in either instance, blaming “mistakes” in its automated content moderation systems (including AI tools that can’t tell the difference between enthusiastic follower engagement and a bot attack).

Mistakes or not, with early voting in the U.S. midterms already underway, these events serve as a stark reminder that all major social media platforms need to have stronger systems in place to ensure that they serve, rather than impede, democratic communication.

content:
Lääkeala on kokoonsa nähden merkittävä toimiala Suomessa. Vaikka ala työllistää alle prosentin yrityssektorin työvoimasta, se tuottaa lähes kymmenen prosenttia yrityssektorin liikevoitoista. Lääkealan työn tuottavuus on myös yli kaksinkertainen yrityssektorin keskiarvoon verrattuna, ilmenee tuoreesta Etla-tutkimuksesta. Lääkealan vienti on kuitenkin keskittynyt voimakkaasti yhteen tuoteryhmään, alkaloidipohjaisiin lääkkeisiin, ja t&k-investoinnit jäävät Suomessa selvästi Ruotsia ja Tanskaa alemmalle tasolle. Tutkimus- ja kehitysinvestointien vahvistamiselle on Suomessa kasvunvaraa.

Lääkeala Suomessa on paitsi korkean teknologian ja osaamisen toimiala, myös kokoonsa nähden taloudellisesti merkittävä toimiala. Ala työllistää alle prosentin yrityssektorin työvoimasta, mutta tuottaa lähes kymmenen prosenttia yrityssektorin liikevoitoista. Myös työn tuottavuus lääkealalla on yli kaksinkertainen yrityssektorin keskiarvoon verrattuna.

Lääkealan ajantasainen tilannekuva on selvitetty tuoreessa Etlan tutkimuksessa Suomen lääkeala: rakenne, kehitys ja taloudellinen merkitys (Etla Raportti 182). Tutkimuksen on rahoittanut Lääketeollisuus ry.

title: Vahva Eurooppa, vaikuttava Suomi: Eurooppalaisen Suomen eduskuntavaali- ja hallitusohjelmatavoitteet 2027–2031
content:
Suomi on vahvasti osa Euroopan unionia ja sen jäsenenä vahvempi kuin yksin. Eurooppalainen elämäntapamme perustuu EU:n arvoihin – demokratiaan, oikeusvaltioon, vapauteen ja ihmisoikeuksiin. Suomi hyötyy jäsenyydestä taloudellisesti, poliittisesti ja turvallisuuden näkökulmasta. 

EU-politiikka on erottamaton osa kansallista politiikkaamme. Euroopan turvallisuusympäristö, globaali valtakamppailu ja unionin tuleva laajentuminen edellyttävät Suomelta aiempaa pitkäjänteisempää, tiiviimpää ja aloitteellisempaa EU-politiikkaa. Suomen etu on toimintakykyinen, demokraattinen ja strategisesti vahva Euroopan unioni, joka kykenee tekemään päätöksiä, puolustamaan itseään ja kansalaisiaan sekä turvaamaan eurooppalaisen talouden ja yhteiskuntien menestyksen muuttuvassa maailmassa. Vain yhtenäinen ja toimintakykyinen Eurooppa pystyy toimimaan maailmassa kestävän tulevaisuuden – esimerkiksi ilmastonmuutoksen ja luontokadon pysäyttämisen – ja sääntöperusteisen yhteistyön puolesta. title: Cities turning climate ambition into action: Climate Budget Summit
content:
The Climate Budget Summit at the EU Regions Week in Brussels brought city leaders, climate experts, and local practitioners to explore how municipalities can turn ambitious climate goals into concrete investments and measurable actions.

The Summit on 14 October 2026 was launched by the Climate-4-CAST project (co-funded by the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme and contributing to thw EUSBSR Policy Area Energy Actions) to emphasise the role of climate budgeting in helping cities align their financial decisions with climate neutrality objectives.

Organised as a partner event of the EU Week of Regions and Cities, it hosted ca. 50 participants sharing experiences and reflecting on practical solutions for including climate considerations in budgeting and governance. The discussion touched upon common challenges, such as how to manage competing priorities, limited resources and political realities. Most participants represented European local and regional authorities, alongside representatives from the European Commission’s DG REGIO, the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme, and the city networks Eurocities, ICLEI and UBC.

title: Five communities around Lobeke National Park set up and mapping!
content:
Since the last post we’ve conducted two fieldwork trips to Lobeke National Park. Fair to say it’s pretty out of the way – three days by 4X4 on mud roads ridden with muddy ravines in the rainy season and clouds of dust in the dry. But for this reason the area is pretty special, monkeys playing and peering down at you even in villages and around the base camp, gorillas commonly spotted along the tracks of forest, elephants meandering around as they please.

The abundance of animals and tight controls on community activities through the conservation service has however certainly created problems – local communities and particularly the Indigenous Baka hunter-gatherers have great fear of entering the forest due to rangers on patrol and so do not have access to the quantity and diversity of forest produce they rely on. That the farmed food that they are now increasingly encouraged to produce is regularly ravaged by monkeys, gorillas, porcupines and elephants leaves them trapped with little ability to get the nutrition they need.

title: Syria's New Reconstruction Fund a Chance for Reform
content:
Syria and the World Bank Group announced on October 18 the creation of the Syria Recovery and Reconstruction Trust Fund, known as START. Run by the World Bank, the fund will pool donor money and private investment to help restore infrastructure and public services, strengthen state institutions, and finance reforms the Syrian government identifies as priorities.

The World Bank estimates Syria’s post-conflict reconstruction will cost about US$216 billion.

Norway pledged approximately 90 million krone ($9.6 million) and the Netherlands €15 million ($16.8 million). START’s initial focus, according to Syria’s state news agency, SANA, is infrastructure, health and education. It will operate under World Bank policies, which include standards on stakeholder engagement, land acquisition, and grievance mechanisms. But those standards only cover START-funded projects and governance arrangements are still being finalized, according to SANA.

title: OPINION: Protecting the Sacred City of Anuradhapura
content:
By Dr. Asoka Bandarage*

COLOMBO. Sri Lanka | 27 October 2026 (IDN) — Buddhism was first introduced to Sri Lanka in Anuradhapura in the 3rd century BCE by Arahant Mahinda, the son of the Indian Emperor Asoka. For nearly 1500 years, Anuradhapura remained Sri Lanka’s capital and the intellectual and spiritual centre of Theravada Buddhism in Asia. The Anuradhapura civilisation achieved unmatched advances in architecture, engineering and urban planning, still evident in its monumental stupas, monasteries, palaces and sophisticated hydraulic and agricultural systems.

Buddhism was gradually assimilated into Hinduism and had disappeared from India by the 12th century CE. The Chola invasion from India and the sacking and conquest in 1017 CE dealt a heavy blow to Buddhist civilisation, ending Anuradhapura’s role as the island’s political capital. The sacred city has continued to face attacks, including the LTTE massacre of 146 devotees at the Sri Maha Bodhi on Vesak full moon, 14 May 1985. Yet Anuradhapura has survived as one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities and as a sacred site that has attracted Buddhist pilgrims over the centuries.

title: A Behind-the-Scenes Look at the Physical Archive
content:
Visitors who came to the open house at the Physical Archive in Richmond, California, on October 20 were curious. They wanted to learn about the range of items collected, the process of preservation, and the staff responsible for making it all happen. 

As people toured the space and observed the various media being saved, many also expressed support and reverence for the Internet Archive’s work to provide universal access to all knowledge.

VIEW PHOTOS FROM THE EVENT

“I really care about preservation and digital culture. Places like this are important to maintaining and building the society we want to live in,” said Sidney Le, a film archivist who now works in logistics, of his third visit to the Physical Archives. “It’s good to see that people here are taking seriously the idea of holding on to culture and preserving it.”

Liz Rosenberg, donations manager for the Archive, welcomed the crowd in Richmond and provided directions for the evening.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: Pelko kasvaa Kabulissa, kun Taliban pidättää naisia huiveista huolimatta
content:
Kabul on naisille pelon kaupunki. Olivatpa he menossa lääkäriin, kauppaan tai tapaamaan sukulaisiaan, perille pääsy on epävarmaa.

He pelkäävät tarkistuspisteitä, talibanien moraalipoliiseja ja pidätetyksi tulemista väärän vaatetuksen tai miespuolisen saattajan puutteen vuoksi.

Monelle naiselle kotoa ulos lähteminen on vaikea päätös. He joutuvat pohtimaan, mitä tapahtuu, jos heidät pidätetään: Pääsenkö palaamaan kotiin? Jos pääsen, onko minulla vielä sama asema perheessä tai yhteisössä?

Syyskuussa talibanien moraalipoliisi pidätti Yhdysvalloissa toimivan afganistanilaisen Amu TV:n mukaan ainakin parikymmentä naista ja tyttöä Taimanissa Kabulissa.

Muutamat heistä kertoivat tulleensa pidätetyiksi, vaikka heillä oli määräysten mukainen päähuivi, hijab, ja poliisin repineen naisten vaatteita näiden päältä kahakassa. Yön yli jatkuneen pidätyksen jälkeen heidät vapautettiin vasta, kun perheet ja paikallisyhteisöt maksoivat takuut.

title: Ei vain kuultavaksi – kohti aitoa osallistamista
content:
Tulevaisuudessa elävien ihmisten mielipiteiden tulisi olla keskeisessä roolissa päätöksenteossa, kun kestävää tulevaisuutta rakennetaan. On selvää, että syntymättömien ihmisten osallistaminen ei ole mahdollista, mutta mielipiteitä täynnä olevia nuoria on paljon.

Nuoria tarvitaan mukaan laajasti koko päätöksenteon kentälle – mutta miten? Yksi selkeä tapa edesauttaa nuorten osallisuutta on tarjota heille enemmän tietoa heidän vaikuttamismahdollisuuksistaan. Tiedon tarjoaminen voi tapahtua esimerkiksi kouluissa, harrastuksissa, nuorisotiloissa tai sosiaalisen median välityksellä. Toisaalta some voi olla itsessään myös hyvä kanava osallistaa nuoria esimerkiksi kyselyiden avulla.

Nuorilla tulee olla arjen asiat kunnossa, jotta he pystyvät toimimaan merkittävässä roolissaan kestävyyssiirtymän toteuttajina. Maaseutupolitiikan KERÄ-verkosto korostaa tulevien eduskuntavaalien alla, että nuorten mahdollisuudet kestävään arkeen, koulutukseen, työhön, asumiseen ja harrastuksiin on turvattava myös maaseudulla. Nuorten yhdenvertaisista mahdollisuuksista huolehtiminen onkin keskeinen osa kestävän tulevaisuuden rakentamista.

title: A Reason for Optimism on US Competition Policy
content:
Mozilla has long called for US antitrust reform in digital markets. After several false starts, real change has yet to materialize. In the meantime, dominant tech players have further entrenched their hold, limiting choice and degrading people’s experiences. Integration of new AI services into existing ecosystems is enabling those same companies to perpetuate and accelerate that power.

But, there’s reason for optimism. Momentum is again building toward antitrust reform, and this time feels different. With support from start ups, middle tech challengers, civil society, and think tanks across the political spectrum – and most importantly, legislative champions in Congress – it’s clear that the time is coming.

This is a debate about how the largest tech companies control the products and innovations in the market, and access to the services the people use every day. At the center are questions about user choice, interoperability, privacy, security and whether independent innovators have an opportunity to compete on merit.

title: Turbulent Times Call For Experimental Law
content:
MUNICH — Shortly after wandering into the Munich Urban Colab this summer, I found myself trying to follow an intense conversation in German about the city’s new experiment with autonomous buses. A local official, clocking my curious puzzlement, offered an aside in English: “We are asking ourselves: ‘What does it mean when the law is an experiment too?’”

No question may be more essential to governance in our era of dangerous uncertainty. 

Global warming is accelerating faster than global treaties on mitigation can be negotiated. Climate catastrophes occur with a sudden ferocity beyond what current adaptation laws anticipate. Biological threats surface and kill before public health responses can be formulated. And AI is evolving faster and more wildly than regulators or lawmakers, or even its designers, expect.

All this dizzying unpredictability is undermining traditional legal structures. The threat is not just to the rule of law, but to the very nature of law, at least as humans have conceived it.

title: ‘Is This Real?’: A Serbian Investigative Journalist Reflects on the Country’s Stunning Election
content:
Sunday’s election marked a turning point in Serbia, with the ruling SNS party of Aleksandar Vučić handed a resounding defeat by a student movement that capitalized on mounting public anger over years of corruption and criminality.

Many of those abuses had been exposed by KRIK, an award-winning Serbian investigative outlet and OCCRP partner that has spent years covering the country’s criminals, its corrupt officials, and the connections between them. In return, its young journalists have withstood pressure most people can scarcely imagine: personal attacks by pro-government tabloids, an endless stream of lawsuits, and even death threats.

Now, a new era is dawning. The seemingly unbreakable control exercised by Vučić — who served as information minister under dictator Slobodan Milošević — has been broken.

In this interview, KRIK editor-in-chief Stevan Dojčinović reflects on what the last few days have meant for him, how the students did it, and what challenges lie ahead. As he spoke with OCCRP late at night, the sounds of celebration filtered in from the street.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

title: How Balzac’s Extreme Coffee Habit Fueled His Productive Writing Routine
content: Even now, in this age when the very reading of literature is endangered — or so the articles tell us — Honoré de Balzac (1799–1850) retains a notable ability to pick up new admirers. But even though he may have a decent readership by the standards of French novelists who died in the middle of the nineteenth century, one does wonder whether he still inspires the kind of devotion embodied by William Hobart Royce. A Brooklyn bookseller’s assistant first introduced to Les Cent Contes drolatiques as an impressionable (and duly scandalized) teenager on a trip to England, Royce became not just the early twentieth century’s foremost American expert on Balzac, but also a kind of clone of the man himself, right down to his appearance.

title: This Oil Company Is Linked to 1,000 Pollution Incidents and Other Violations. Oklahoma Never Punished It.
content:
In June 2023, staff at an Oklahoma regulatory agency were fed up. The state isn’t known for cracking down on oil and gas companies for polluting the environment, but for over a year, the staff had been building a case to punish Citation Oil & Gas, one of the nation’s largest privately owned oil companies. 

About 30 miles north of the Texas border, toxic wastewater was gushing from the ground outside the small city of Ardmore. In the mile-wide oil field known as the Bayou, an oily sheen glistened on creeks and long streaks of salt scarred the land. The so-called purges, bubbling up among stands of oak and walnut trees, also threatened drinking water sources, drawing attention from the Environmental Protection Agency, according to a federal report.

State investigators pinned the blame on Citation’s injection wells, which pump wastewater from oil production back underground at high pressures and volumes in order to produce more oil. But this injection came with risks.

title: Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton asiantuntijalausunto: RTS 26:25 Asuntoyhtiön linjasaneeraushanke
content:
Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto kiittää mahdollisuudesta lausua asuntoyhtiön linjasaneeraushanketta käsittelevästä ohjekorttiehdotuksesta. Ohjekortissa on esitetty kattavasti ja selkeästi linjasaneeraushankkeen eteneminen ja vastuut teknisestä näkökulmasta. Linjasaneeraushankkeeseen voi kuitenkin liittyä merkittäviä rakennussuojelukysymyksiä. Lisäksi rakennuksissa voi olla merkittäviä arkkitehtonisia arvoja, vaikka niillä ei olisi suojelumerkintää.

Linjasaneeraushanke koskee tyypillisesti rakennusten sisäpuolisia osia, jolloin merkittävimmät rakennussuojelukysymykset koskevat useimmissa tapauksissa porrashuoneita ja niihin kohdistuvia muutoksia. Tulevaisuudessa linjasaneeraushankkeissa saatetaan toteuttaa myös esimerkiksi paikallista energiantuotantoa, kuten katolle sijoitettavia aurinkopaneeleja. Tällöin linjasaneeraushakkeen suojeluharkinta voi koskea myös esimerkiksi vesikattoa ja julkisivun osia. Rakennushistoriaselvitys on hyvä työkalu arvojen selvittämiseen ja siinä voidaan keskittyä hankkeen ja rakennuksen kannalta keskeisiin kysymyksiin. Näin hankkeen tavoitteet ja reunaehdot ovat selvät kaikille osapuolille hankkeen alusta alkaen sujuvoittaen hankkeen toteutusta kokonaisuutena.

title: Seuran jäsen, hae mukaan työryhmien toimintaan!
content:
Työryhmätoiminta on Kirjastoseuran suola!

Etsimme nyt työryhmiin uusia jäseniä kaudelle 2027–28. Suomen kirjastoseurassa toimii vuonna 2026 kuusi työryhmää. Työryhmiin voit tutustua täällä. Lisätietoja työryhmien toiminnasta saat kunkin ryhmän puheenjohtajalta.

Työryhmiin etsitään jälleen uusia jäseniä. Samalla lomakkeella haetaan sekä työryhmän varsinaiseksi että opiskelijajäseneksi. Huomaathan, että koulutus-ja tutkimustyöryhmän suuren koon vuoksi ryhmään ei valita tällä hakukierroksella täysin uusia edustajia.

Työryhmätoiminta tarjoaa seuran jäsenille mahdollisuuksia verkostoitua, oppia ja kehittää asiantuntijuuttaan. Se tarjoaa vaikuttamiskanavan (suomalaiseen) kirjastotyöhön, auttaa tutustumaan kirjastokenttään valtakunnallisesti ja ryhmässä toimimisesta saa työtodistuksen. Käytännön toimintaan ryhmät saavat apua ja tukea myös seuran toimistolta.

Työryhmän tehtäviä ovat:

  • toimia Kirjastoseuran hallituksen tukena antaen asiantuntija-apua
  • edistää yhdenvertaisuutta ja moninaisuutta kirjastoalalla
  • tukea ammattitaitoa järjestämällä koulutuspäiviä ja ammattitapaamisia sekä tarjoamalla mahdollisuuksia vertaistukeen

content:
Tack till alla som i år sökt bidrag för studieresor i grupp inom utbildningssektorn eller för språkmöten. Ni var så många och era ansökningar var så bra att våra budgetmedel nu är slut. Vi har därför tillfälligt stängt de här två ansökningarna.

Varje år i oktober gör vi en budget för alla våra nästan 50 olika bidragsformer. Då uppskattar vi bland annat hur mycket ni kommer att ansöka om inom varje bidragsform under det kommande året. title: AI sell-off would rattle global economy, EU watchdog warns
content:
PARIS — Investors piling into a small number of mega technology companies could have a “significant impact” on the economy if the artificial intelligence bet doesn’t pay off, the head of the EU’s financial markets watchdog said.

Verena Ross, who is set to step down as chair of the European Securities and Markets Authority at the end of October, said in an interview that the “significant concentration of market value” in a few companies “raises some questions around how to ensure proper diversification of investor portfolios.”

Ross was speaking the day after American AI giant Anthropic filed paperwork to take the company public in what could be the biggest listing in history, but also a test of investor confidence in the current AI boom. She said finance regulators worldwide are watching “the gap between the valuation issue and the macro picture.”

title: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
content:
It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t

Think back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up, Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI. And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

title: Serbia’s leaderless student movement has won a historic election – but what happens next?
content:
Serbia’s leaderless anti-corruption coalition, the Student List, defeated the group led by former president Aleksandar Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) by a comfortable margin in October 25 elections.

Their 53.3% of the vote should get them 141 seats in parliament, well clear of the 125 seats needed to form a majority. The SNS can be a loud but ineffectual opposition with the 103 seats netted by their 39.7% of the vote.

The result was known shortly after polls closed, with Vučić conceding defeat 90 minutes later. Once the celebrations settle down, it looks as if Serbia will manage a peaceful transfer of power to a democratically elected government.

Read more: ‘We changed the system’: how Serbian students ended Alexander Vučić’s 12 years in power

This was not inevitable. By mid-afternoon on election day, news outlets were reporting concentrations of armoured police vehicles and movements of personnel at various spots in central Belgrade.

title: The female scream is now an all-powerful cry in horror films
content:
As Halloween approaches and screen audiences are saturated with the sights and sounds of screaming women in horror films and TV shows, it’s a great time to look at the women whose vocal artistry created genuinely effective screams on screen.

Behind every memorable cinematic scream lies a vocal performance that is often reduced to a natural, unreflective outburst. But that assessment obscures the women behind its most powerful manifestations. For example, think of the work of Shelley Duvall in The Shining, Janet Leigh in Psycho or Toni Collette in Hereditary.

Certain screen actors have made the scream their calling card to fame and notoriety, under the designation “scream queen.” These queens are the unsung heroes of the horror industry through their dedication to the vocal performance of the fear and terror in the many guises of horror.

As onscreen horror proliferated in the 1970s, the term “scream queen” became popular, most notably through Calvin Beck’s 1978 book Scream Queens: Heroines of the Horrors. Later, in popular culture, “scream queen” applied to “any female star who has made a career playing women who survive extreme trauma or peril.”
